notes.note: 19 tackles and 29 disposals with a fantastic game for Berry.

Cook is continuing to provide us with some great value and good scoring. 15 disposals and a goal and he is a good user of the footy which helps his score. His BE is in the 70s now which means his money growth is at its limit
Solid from Cook with 22 disposals and 7 marks. He is still beating that BE and he is a safe to play on field. The hope is we can get him through to the byes.
The winning goal from Cook certainly helped boost his score but he had a good game as well with 21 disposals.  Nothing to worry about here he is still making money and is fieldable.
Cook continues to post some great scores and is very fieldable for you. 20 disposals and importantly he has good job security. His BE is still low so keep playing him.
This was the best for the year for Cook which will see his value rise nicely for a couple of weeks. 19 touches and a goal at a very handy 89% efficiency. He has been a great pick up.
Cook has had three in the 60s now and this looks to be his range now which whilst his BE is still low at 41 is fine to keep holding and he is safe for on field.
10 kicks and no handballs for Cook with a goal. This was his lowest score so far this season but far from concerning. He is scoring very well and still has a great BE.

Many coaches downgraded Petracca to Cook and that proved to be a great play with this score boosting his value and ensuring he will make more cash in coming weeks with a BE of -12. 21 disposals and 6 marks in the wet was a good result.
Cook couldn't back up last week's big outing as things were a little tighter against the Dogs. But he still posted a score that means he has a great BE that will see him a heavy trade in this week.
Cook was fantastic and deserved the hype he was given over recent weeks. 21 disposals to go with a goal. He will be a popular trade in
Curtin injured a kneecap in the preseason so rule him out of your squads.
Dawson was the top scorer in the game with his 24 touches goal and 6 marks. He was back in the CBAs with 63% this week which is more than the last two games combined.
Dawson returned this week and put the Crows on his back at stages and ended with 12 marks 29 disposals and a goal. Look for him to hopefully continue with this form.
Dawson returned and was massive. He was taking kick ins as well as kicking 2 goals for his 28 disposals. He didn't spend as much time at CBAs at just 29%. His best score for the year.
Dawson posted his lowest so far this season and he couldn't get the space he wanted in the wet. Nothing to be concerned about here yet.
Dawson returned this week and slotted two goals to go with 23 disposals. He showed no signs of the injury that held him out last week.
Dawson missed this week but had it not been for the short turnaround could have played so hold him. He participated fully at training on Tuesday so it looks like he should be fine.
Dawson had a great second half and really dragged the Crows back into the game and this was reflected in his score. If not for his 64% efficiency he would have had a big score.
Dawson wasn't at his very best but did enough for us with his 21 touches. He did land very heavily on his back in the last minutes of the game but did get up.
Edwards dropped down from last week's score with just 12 disposals and only 6 were effective. With a BE of -24 he is still one you could downgrade to but that 39 does ring some alarms..
First game for Charlie did see 3 free kicks against but he also had 18 disposals and 5 clearances. If he can put up another game like this he is likely to be a popular trade in.
Laird injured a calf early in the game but did finish it out. He will miss 1 to 2 weeks.

McAndrew had a good day against Xerri and took the honour by virtue of his 2 goals but he sat on the pine for much of the last term when the game was well and truly over which did limit him to just 9 points in that term.
McAndrew dominated the hit outs against Balta with 33 to go with 9 disposals and a goal. He made his BE and with a new one of 53 he looks like we can hold til his bye.
McAndrew had a solid outing against Sweet with 11 disposals and 33 hit outs. With Richmond this week he should post a good score and beat his BE.

McAndrew had 30 hitouts and 11 disposals but at just 36% efficiency. He beat his BE but now has a BE of 73 so it could be time to upgrade him to one of the big two. He shouldn't drop sharply but he needs to be watched closely.

McAndrew got off to a slow start but finished well with 9 disposals and 29 hitouts against Marshall after TDK copped an early injury. His BE is still low at 51 but it won't be long before we need to either see another big game or trade out of him.
McAndrew didn't have it his own way against the stronger Pittonet. But he still did more than enough and remains a good R2 option.
McAndrew wasn't impacted at all by O'Brien being in the team and he made a statement with his best score of the season laying 13 tackles. He is looking like he could be a permanent R2 at this stage.
McAndrew continues to impress and importantly generate cash. Not his best score but also the conditions weren't friendly to big men. 40 hitouts and 17 disposals was a good return.
McAndrew had a great game against English with 38 hit outs and 13 disposals. As an R2 selection he is certainly paying off.
McAndrew was the R2 for many teams and he was great with 27 hitouts and 13 disposals. He did this against good opposition with Cameron before he faces English this week. This role is his for now.
McAndrew seems to have taken the number one ruck spot from O'Brien
Milera had just the 19 disposals but with the Crows in total control the ball wasn't in his area a great deal and the pressure wasn't there.
Milera was the second highest scorer in the game from his 32 disposals largely thanks to his efficiency of 94%. A great performance and his second over 120 in a row.
Milera had his third highest score of the season with 29 disposals at 93%. He has been a great hold for those that kept him after his two low scores.
Milera's lowest in the last four as the Lions had control of the game. He should be better this week against the Power.
Milera top scored for the Crows and has now put together 3 over 100 since many teams traded him out. 29 disposals at 93% and 9 marks.
Milera has now posted back to back over 100 with 25 disposals this week which included 5 kick ins which is the most he has had since round 1.
Milera showed some of the form we saw in round 1 with the best score for the Crows this week with 27 disposals at 92% efficiency.

Milera faded out of the game in the last term and didn't look to be at his best. Unfortunately his BE has risen to 137 as that first game washes out from his cycle so he is one you should try and trade out this week.
Milera had just 2 of the kick ins this week after taking 14 last week. Hopefully this is just a one off as the Crows back line was under real pressure.
Milera had his best game for a while as he racked up 34 disposals at 94% efficiency. Could this be his year!
O'Brien came into the side but played just 35% time on ground with 3 disposals and 15 hitouts. He had no impact on McAndrew's output.
O'Brien looks like he is set for extended stints in the SANFL with McAndrew looking like the preferred ruck option at Adelaide.

Rachele had his second in the 80s in a row and was right on his BE but it did take 3 goals to get there. His CBAs were at just 9% which isn't ideal and he may be one we trade at the byes. This isn't the role we were promised for him.
Rachele spent a lot of time up forward attending just 15% of CBAs which isn't the role we want. But he did end with 2 goals from his 14 touches which boosted his score.
2 goals 3 for Rachele as this is now three in a row of 70 points or less for him. A huge concern for owners as he is losing value. The Crows have a good run to their bye so he should rebound.

Rachele has struggled now in the last two games with 15 disposals this week making it two poor scores in a row now. This is a real concern as we saw his CBAs drop down to 38% after 81% the week before.
Rachele couldn't back up last week's big scoring. Just 20 disposals and a goal for him. This is going to happen so don't panic on him.

Rachele has been on fire over the last three weeks ads he equalled the 127 he posted two weeks ago. He had just the 48% CBAs this week which is his second lowest of the season but the 4 goals were the key.
Rachele was again good and had 65% CBAs with his 19 disposals. If you need to get a forward he is one you can't go past. This is back to back weeks of CBAs in the mid 60s.
This was one of the best games we have seen Rachele play as he top scored for the Crows with a team high 7 clearances to go with 31 disposals. With Dawson out he attended 64% of the CBAs.
Rachele gave away 5 free kicks which really hurt his scoring. He had 18 disposals and 2 goals but the free kicks and 9 clangers make him someone that we may look at trading out.
Rachele managed 24 touches and a goal for a solid score as he had the role we want with 50% CBAs. The key will be what happens when Rankine returns next game.

Had the tag early but once the game was done in the second he was released and ended with a game high in contested possessions and clearances with 15 and 10. This is the role we knew he would excel in. Best to wait til after R12 though.

Rankine was massive and dominated the game. 10 marks 9 tackles and 33 disposals to go with a goal. He does have a tricky run coming up with tags from Simpkin and Mullin a night game in Tasmania and a bye.
Rankine is certainly looking back to his best. He had 23 disposals and a goal and if not for that R12 bye he would be a great trade in.
This was more like Rankine. 11 contested possessions and 19 disposals with a couple of goals. This is now two good ones in the last three. He is starting to get back to the form we like to see.
1 goal 3 behinds for Rankine from his 20 disposals but it was the 40% efficiency that hurt his score. Just one score over 70 now in the last 4 isn't really what we were hoping for.

This is the Rankine that we were all expecting to see this season. 2 goals 7 tackles with 22 disposals. His BE is at 92 so you can hold off if you need to as his price shouldn't move upwards a significant amount this week without a huge score.
Rankine struggled again but was better than the previous week. 14 disposals and 3 behinds for him. His BE is still very high so we can watch him for another couple of weeks.
Rankine was tagged by Mullin and really didn't look at his best. He had 7 disposals 1 goal but gave away 3 free kicks. His price will plummet with a BE of 207 so don't go near him for a while.
Rankine returned to the team from his suspension and was quiet for the first half but did start to get into the game in the last where he kicked an important goal that boosted his score.
Rankine will miss round one through suspension
Worrell has had now 4 games over 100 for the season with another great game this week. 11 marks and 28 disposals at 92% as he is putting his hand up for a spot in our teams.
Andrews will be missing until Gather round after an errant swinging arm has seen him suspended for 3 games.

Annable didn't have a big outing in his first game despite 13 disposals. Just the 2 were contested and 240m gained. We can wait another week yet but another game like this will mean he is a correction trade.
We didn't see Annable in the Opening round clash so keep him as a downgrade target later
24 touches for Will but just 79% efficiency and his lowest since round 5
23 touches for Ashcroft and his lowest in the last month. We shouldn't be concerned as he is still scoring but he will need to be upgraded over the byes.
Will didn't have a huge day as the Lions spread the points around with 12 players on 90 or more. He ended with 28 disposals and 9 marks but his efficiency let him down.
26 disposals and a goal but 3 frees against meant that he had his second under 100 in a row.
Ashcroft had Simpkin for company for much of the game and was held to 19 disposals and his lowest for the season.
Will Ashcroft had his own footy and it looks to be his midfield now. 36 disposals and a goal for his best for the season by far.
Bailey has been a popular pick in recent weeks with some big scores but this week he had just the 14 disposals and didn't kick any goals. His second lowest score this year.
Berry was the top scorer in the game and best with 31 disposals and 10 marks. He has had one good and one poor score before this so he isn't a solid play just yet.
2 goals but just the 8 disposals. This was Charlie's lowest in the last four. His scoring can be quite up and down.
Kiddy had the 18 disposals and a good efficiency at 88%. This makes it 6 weeks without triple figures for him.
Coleman put up 19 disposals and 7 marks but again missed his BE. You could be forgiven for upgrading him. He has 61 as a BE which is still achievable
Coleman was on the cusp of being traded out by a lot of sides but he stood up and took 11 marks and had 24 disposals.

Coleman had a poor day by the standards we have seen recently as Lincoln McCarthy took some of his points this week. This is now two poor ones in the last three and his BE at 78 means we may need to look at moving him on.
Coleman continues to deliver with his 20 disposals and 7 marks this week. He is showing us some solid form which we all knew he had in him.
Back to the scores from his early games for Coleman which is a concern for owners. His BE of 30 means we can wait still before we need to consider whether we trade him out.
Kiddy was great again this week with his 22 touches and 10 marks. His best for the season so far and he is looking fantastic. Well done for those that held.
This was what we were hoping for from Coleman with his 21 disposals coming at 85% efficiency. He is now at a BE of 7 so hold him.
Coleman was disappointing but the Lions weren't good. His BE of 22 means we could hold him and don't forget he is on bye this week.
Coleman did enough but his time on ground was low at just 74%. No reason to not select him though.
Draper still has just the one big score this season even though this was better than last week. He had a solid game but really isn't up there with the best of the rucks this season.
Draper struggled again this week to score. He isn't an option.
Draper's first game for the Lions was a forgettable one with 3 behinds and just 8 hitouts and 8 disposals.
Dunkley  led the Lions in Contested possessions and clearances for the week from his 22 disposals. This is back to back 80s now.
Dunkley wasn't his usual influential self with 15 of his 23 by hand. He isn't on our radar.
Dunkley's last two games have been better than opening round and he is still an option for us to keep an eye on.
Much better for Dunkley this week. 9 tackles to go with his 22 disposals. His price is going to drop and if we need to pick someone up after his bye we could consider him a fallen premium.
A quiet opening round for Dunkley. His price will fall so no need to rush him into your side.
Jaspa had one out of the box with his 10 marks and 27 disposals. Is this the break out game that will spark his run. Keep an eye on him.
McCluggage had a quiet game with just the 16 disposals and only half were contested. This was his second in the 60s since his return. Importantly his TOG went up again.

McCluggage led the game in clearances with 11 and had the third most contested possessions with 13. This was his first over 100 and he did all this in 77% TOG which is the most he has had this season.
McCluggage is building and was again good this week with 9 clearances and 12 contested possessions.
McCluggage's return hasn't heralded huge scores and he is still one that you don't need to consider unless he starts going on a tear.
McCluggage struggled in his second game back. His BE has stayed high at 185 so he is off the table for us for a while to come.
McCluggage returned to the side with 20 disposals. We need to see more from him before we look to bring him in. Particularly with a BE of 282.
Hugh left the opening round game in the first quarter with a calf injury. Watch the injury reports to see when he may return.
Neale had the tag from Mullin but he still had 28 disposals to be the second best scorer for the Lions. Just his second under 100 in the last 7 games.

Neale topped the disposals for the game with 33 as he also took 8 marks and had 9 clearances. This makes it 5 over 110 in the last 6 for him as he is really looking a good unique pick with less than 10% of teams owning him.
Neale finished with a goal and 27 disposals but it was his first under 110 in the last five.
Huge day for Neale with 42 disposals and 13 marks after he left the game very early from a heavy bump to the chest.
Neale was one of the best for the lions in his 300th as he led the game in Contested possessions and clearances with 16 and 10. A good run of 3 games now.
Neale was the top scorer for the game with 30 disposals 20 contested disposals and 10 clearances to lead those two categories in the game.
First 100+ score since opening round for Lachie who looked a lot better this week than he has over recent games. He looked to be playing a with deal of freedom
This was a very quiet one from Neale with his 19 disposals being his lowest amount of touches for the season by 9.
Neale was still one of the best for the Lions despite the score. 28 disposals for him as he had the second most touches in the game.
Neale was the top possession getter in the game. Looked good to go for another great season.
Wilmott put up his second over 100 in the last three weeks and he was the only Lion over 100. In recent weeks it has just been that 55 in round 9 that has been a bump in the road.
Wilmot was huge with 12 marks and 32 disposals. Easily his best of the year. But hold off until we see another game of this standard with his previous 5 only averaging 77.6
ZZ was a late inclusion for Fort which hurt a number of teams who used him as a Loop captain this week. He rose in value which is what we have been waiting for.
Solid from ZZ and just the score those that had him at R3 would have been looking for.
Zorko was a late out 'managed' so just watch to see if it was something more serious.
19 disposals for Zorko and just the 4 marks. This is well down for him and it was his worst score this year apart from the game he was injured in.
Zorko returned and it was like he hadn't left with 13 marks to go with 27 disposals and the third most points for the Lions. His BE tells us we can wait another week with a BE of 148.
Keep an eye on teams there is talk he could be back soon.
We saw Zorko leave the game in the second term with a calf injury that looks like he is going to miss a few weeks. He is  going to need to be a trade.

Zorko took 9 marks with his 28 disposals. He didn't get to his BE however his price won't fluctuate too much as his scoring is quite consistent in this range. He is going to be someone to have on your watch list.
Zorko had his lowest so far this year but there were only 5 players in this game over 100 so nothing to be concerned about. His efficiency was what caused the low score at 60%.
Zorko was the best for the Lions with his 30 disposals and 11 marks. The ball was in his area with the Swans pressing and he is still someone we could pivot to after his bye.
Zorko continues to defy his age with a huge game to be the best for the Lions. We saw no reason that he won't be a great selection again this season.
Cerra's second game was better than the first with 7 tackles included but he isn't doing enough to make us consider him.
Cripps starred with 29 disposals and 2 goals whilst leading the game in contested possessions and clearances. Back to back 100+ for the first time this year.
This was Cripps best score this season but it was also just his third over 100. Of his 32 disposals only 9 were kicks. He did have team high 9 clearances and 18 contested possessions.
Cripps continues with his higher handball to kick ratio. 7 kicks to 18 handballs. Second lowest score of the season for him despite his 5 clearances which was an equal team high.
Cripps spent some time on the bench at a crucial point but his game was solid with 29 disposals and 9 tackles. But 4 free kicks against hurt his score. His value is dropping so you can wait on him.
Cripps was in his handball heavy game again with 2/3rds of his disposals being b hand. He was under pressure with 15 contested possessions and an efficiency of just 57%.
Cripps was one of the best for the Blues with this a good turn around from last week. His scoring can be up and down as he was aided by 19 of his 32 disposals being contested.
Cripps was trying to lead his team from the front but this game was one that shows he has a wide scoring range. Not one for your starting team.
Dean posted what is his best for the last four games but still not enough for us to have him. His BE is at 35 with an average over the last 5 of 42 it is just about time to trade.
Dean continues to leak cash with an 8 disposal game this week. He must be moved out of your side.
Dean continues to struggle to score and is a must trade out.
Dean had just 6 disposals and 4 marks with this his lowest score of the year. His BE has risen to 53 and he is unfieldable. Move him on.
Hewett has been up and down with his scoring this season and isn't showing what we saw in previous years. However he was one of just two Blues over 100 this week. Hold if you have him.
This is now two scores in the 70s from Hewett which is a concern for owners. He had just the 18 disposals.
Hewett was the best scorer for the Blues as he is looking in for another good season.
Ollie was the top scorer for the Blues with a solid efficiency of 87% for his 23 disposals and 9 marks. His scoring is too erratic though to be one we need to get in.
Ison's debut was a very tidy one with 15 disposals and 5 marks. One more game like this and he will be a very popular downgrade option.
This was Newman's lowest score for the season with his 21 disposals conceding 3 free kicks against.
Newman was the top scoring Blue in the game with his 13 marks and 28 disposals. He is certainly worth considering if he can score like this.
Newman had a great first half but when the Blues started to struggle so did he. He did end with 24 disposals but if the Blues get it together he is one to consider.
Newman's second game was another in the 90s. His BE is at 75 so he will rise in value with a good score this week.
Newman was a popular choice until he was suspended in preseason. He ended with a goal and 19 disposals with 9 marks. He didn't blow us away but he certainly put himself back on our radar.
Newman is missing for another couple of games through suspension. We will see him again after round 2.
Pittonet returned but was no match for De Koning and Marshall registering his worst of the season.
Pittonet suffered a hand injury which will see him come out of the side this week at least.
Pittonet was the best scorer for the Blues as he was up against Trembath and CCJ and ended with a couple of goals as well.
Pittonet backed up his good opening round game. He seems to be one that is adapting to the new rules for ruck men well
Pittonet was the clear number one over Reidy and his score was elevated by 3 goals. Not sure he is the one you want as a ruck on field.
Reidy suffered with Pittonet back as he played just 50% time on ground for 6 disposals and 8 hit outs. He isn't rosterable.
Reidy had a great score and has a great BE but just beware as he will be impacted heavily if Pittonet returns and may not hold his spot.
Reidy was dropped pregame and hopefully you saw this in time. Being dropped for the second game is enough to say he shouldn't be in your side.

Smith has had his two best scores in the last 7 games over the last two weeks. He had 52% CBA which is an increase and the most we have seen from him in the last four games so hopefully we see more of this.
Jagga had his best score since round 1 with his 25 disposals at 88% and goal this week. This along with his already low BE will kick start some more cash generation so well done if you held.

Jagga got to his BE comfortably with his best score in the last four games. He is flirting with needing to be traded out. If he can stay in this scoring range you can keep him but be ready to move him at a moments notice.
Smith had 19 disposals and it was his best in the last three. His BE is now at 47 and he probably has one more week in your team.

Jagga beat his BE this week but not by a lot. His scoring is starting to slow and his new BE of 62 means you can now move him on if you want but his scoring should be consistent in this range if you have other issues.
Smith had a tough night with a very quiet first half. But he did bring it home for us. His BE is at 52 so we can hold. The conditions didn't suit him and should be better against the Pies.
17 disposals and a goal for Jagga. Not a big score but we need to remember he is a rookie as he will be still rising in value on the back of this.
Jagga didn't reach the heights but the Blues were poor after half time. He still managed 25 disposals and a goal which was a good return. Nothing to be concerned about here.
We waited a long time to get Smith into our sides after all planning to start him last year and he did not disappoint with the third best score for the Blues from 32 disposals. A must have.

Smith's long awaited debut showed why everyone has talked him up as he got plenty of the footy with 27. Most of this was in the first half when the Blues were on top but he is still a must have in every team.
Wals had a quiet first half with just 26 points but came home with a wet sail to have 8 kicks and 17 handballs.
Walsh racked up 29 disposals as he put last week's low score behind him. Although this was his first back to back weeks under 100.
Walsh was hot early but couldn�t keep going. This was his first sub 90 score of the season.
Walsh was the best for the Blues and it was his highest score of the season. 32 disposals with a goal. He is scoring well and hasn't dropped below 90 yet so a great selection.
Walsh had a quiet first quarter but was good after that. His scoring has been quite consistent so far this season. A solid option.
Walsh had a big first term but was watched a bit closer after that. 8 tackles 8 kicks to go with 21 handballs. The only Blue to go over 100 this week.
Walsh posted his lowest for the year with his goal and 19 disposals. He was one of 6 Blues over 90 this week so his score wasn't as bad as it could have been given the context of the game.
Walsh continued his good start to the year with his 31 disposals and 6 tackles. A great pick and one that we want to keep.

Walsh was off to a brilliant start with a big first half. He did slow down after half time ending with 30 disposals. Still he got through the game and will be one to have on your watchlist if you didn't start him.
Walsh was looking fit after his best preseason in a while. Top scoring for the Blues he was slowed a little when he got the Jordon tag but still nothing to say we shouldn't pick him.
Anderson made his BE and posted his best score in the last three games. He should be good this week as it is a 20 dropping from his scoring cycle and his BE dropped to 5.
Solid outing from Anderson after last week's poor score. 15 disposals and a goal for him as he is still a good hold but keep a watch on his scoring.

This could be it for Angry with his 8 disposals and goal. He missed his BE which is predominantly due to the 5 free kicks that he gave away. His new BE of 28 means he needs to get back to his previous scoring
2 goals for Anderson along with 14 disposals and 4 tackles. He has been consistent in his first three games which is exactly what we want from a rookie. He is still a valid trade in with a BE of -30.
Anderson will be the most popular trade in this week with his BE at -75 after his second game came with 17 disposals. Being a mature aged player he has the bigger body and looks comfortable .
Darcy copped a few knocks in the game and may miss some time potentially. He battled to 14 disposals and 12 hit outs. Could be time to trade if he misses.
Cameron couldn't take advantage of the inexperienced Bomber rucks. 17 hitouts and 15 disposals but his lowest in the last three.
Cameron backed up last week's good game with another. 20 hit outs and 18 disposals for him as he won the battle with Pittonet around the ground.

After two very quiet games we have seen Cameron come back to his best to have the third top score for the Pies. This did surprise us as he came up against Jackson. Hopefully this is the turn of form for him.
Cameron posted his second 59 in a row as he is still struggling to score with these new rules. He is also still splitting time with Oscar Steene.
Cameron had his hands full with the young Crow ruck as he was beaten in the hitouts and had to rely on his around the ground play.
Cameron was solid against TDK. Look for him to be a solid scorer again this season.
Josh had 25 disposals and his second in the 80s in a row.
Daicos  took a back seat to Houston this week finishing with 23 disposals but his score was helped with the 91% efficiency. He is still a valid option.
Daicos had 35 disposals with 8 marks for his first over 100 since round 3.
Lowest for the season for Josh this week. 26 touches for him but with Houston being better it did impact Josh's touches.
Josh Daicos is putting together a start to the season that is making us sit up and look. His BE is sitting around his average so you won't have to get him in straight away if you want him.
Josh Daicos still had a distributor role but had to do a bit more with his brother out of the team. He racked up 25 touches but his equal lowest this year. He is still a very good pick.
Josh Daicos repaid all those that had faith in him this week with 33 disposals and 8 marks. There was a concern to his shoulder early but played out the game and was ok.
Josh Daicos managed 28 disposals as he seems to have a role that is more up the ground than last year as he attended 33% CBAs this week.
Josh was the top scorer for the Pies as they were able to do as they pleased across half back. 13 marks for he and Maynard was nice to see from a scoring point of view.
Daicos got the tag from Jordon as everyone expected. He did manage to still kick 2 goals and have 28 disposals but his efficiency was affected being at just 60%.

Nick copped the Mullin tag as we expected and was held to his lowest score of the season but it wasn't due to low possessions as he had 29 but it was the pressure causing a low 55% efficiency and 9 clangers.
Very quiet first half from Nick but he really got going after half time. 34 disposals and a goal with 10 contested possessions. Watch out for the Osin Mullin tag this week.
Nick took a while to get going and his 44 disposals included 8 clearances but his disposal efficiency was well down at 59% which really impacted his score this week.

Daicos was huge in his 100th. He took the game away from Carlton with a great 10 min burst at the start of the last which really boosted his score. He may not get a great deal cheaper even with a 146 BE so now is the time to buy if you haven't already.
Nick returned this week and didn't look to have any concerns from his calf. He racked up 31 disposals and 4 marks which did result in his lowest this year but nothing to worry about.
Nick failed a pregame fitness test on his corked calf and was a very late out. With an 8 day break he should be good for next week.
Nick was fantastic posting 36 disposals and leading the team in contested possessions and clearances. If you don't have him yet you must get him.
Nick wasn't hard tagged and had 33 disposals but his efficiency was just 63% this week. With a bye this week he is one you can jump on ahead of round 3.
Nick did what Nick does and that is find the footy with 41 disposals. He scored pretty much right on his priced at value. It is certainly still a solid play to start him.

Houston played a bit of second fiddle to Josh Daicos with just 17 disposals at 64%. This was his lowest since round 5. The small ground can slow the scoring of some of the outside runners that aren't used to it
Houston had a quiet first half but came home with 56 points in the second half. We need him to keep this as his floor.  He improved his output after Moore was ruled out.
This was possibly the best game we have seen from Houston at Collingwood. 32 disposals and 7 marks. First back to back over 100 weeks for him.
27 disposals and 8 marks for Dan with this his second best score. He is bouncing around with his scoring as we see different strategies in that Collingwood backline.

Houston was better but still not delivering the big scores we were seeing early in the season. He is still a hold though as there are plenty of other things we should do first like upgrading those rookies.

3 goals 3 behinds for Jez this week with 8 marks. His scoring over the last month has been good for a key position player.
Cameron kicked 3 early goals but was quiet in the second half as the supply dried up. Just 9 disposals at 55% for him. This is always the risk of a key forward.
Cameron was fantastic booting 10 goals from 10 marks and 18 disposals. A huge score which we won't get every week but he is more than capable of delivering these on occasion.
Despite 3 goals we didn't see a huge score from Cameron. We know this can be the case for key forwards.
Cameron did take a big hit early which took the wind out of him. He didn't kick any goals from his 10 kick 1 handball game with this quite a poor score by his standards.
Looking like a elevating his game as he top scored for the Cats with no CBAs in the game against the Suns.
Edwards struggled and had just 56% time on ground and in that time he gave away 4 free kicks.
Edwards left the game to get his ankle restriped in the first quarter and really struggled after that with just 5 disposals and only 2 of them were effective.
Edwards struggled in his second game with just 6 disposals and 12 hit outs in 45% game time. Not one for us.
Edwards was selected by teams as their bench ruck but was well beaten by Jackson and Darcy. As a rookie we can't expect too much from him.
Holmes was one of 7 Cats over 100 from his 26 disposals and 9 contested possessions. He has now alternated over and under 100 over the last four weeks.
33 disposals for Holmes as he was playing the distributor role. His score was held back a little as just 6 contested possessions and 2 clearances.
Holmes was the star for the Cats having 29 disposals at 89% and 2 goals. He set the win up from the midfield and registered his best and 5th over 120 this year.

25 disposals for Holmes but just 68% efficiency as the game was a high pressure one. This was his first sub 100 scoring game for the season. Nothing to worry about as the Cats won't be down like this too often.
Holmes came home strong to finish with 28 disposals as he has still yet to dip below 100 and has had just 1 below 110.
Holmes had a bit or work on his hamstring on the sidelines but it wasn't serious as he ended with 34 disposals in his role sweeping across the half back line. He is in a great patch of form.
Holmes is having a great and consistent start to the season. He is someone you must have in your side. 21 of his 27 this week were kicks.

Holmes was a popular selection for coaches this week and he paid off big with 27 disposals and a goal making it a hat trick of 100+ scores to start the season. He is looking to be a must have this year.
Holmes is one of the elite midfielders in the game and one that we will no doubt be wanting in our midfield by season's end. 32 disposals for him which was the most in the game.
Holmes was good and again could be a solid selection as he looks to continue last year's form.
Mannagh had a night with 5 goals and 30 disposals. He has been up and down over the last few weeks and has posted some really low scores. We need to see consistency before we look to pick him up.
Miers returned this week and finished with the 16 disposals. His BE rose and price will fall so no need to be looking at him yet.
There was talk that Miers had done an ACL but was still playing but this turned out to not be true. But he is still carrying something. Keep a close eye on injuries and team sheets.
This is a couple in the 70s in a row now for Miers which is a concern for those that brought him in. He now has dropped in value so you may want to wait a while if you want him.
Miers was under an injury cloud before the game and it showed early. Thankfully he had a good second half to end with his 22 disposals.

Miers was one of the popular choices to go to from Petracca and he paid off with a big last quarter ending with 8 tackles and 25 disposals in the wet. He only just went past his BE so could still be an option this week.
Miers joined the party with the Cats win as he used the footy well and looked much better than last week. A safe selection with this form.
An interrupted preseason for Miers with a thumb injury and we didn't see any CBAs for him against GC.
Smith was the highlight for the Cats with 34 disposals 11 tackles and 2 goals. He has been putting up some very big scores and should be a target for you as soon as possible.
Huge last term from Smith as he finished with the top score in the game from 40 disposals including 14 contested possessions and 6 clearances. Big bounce back from Bailey.
Smith has Simpkin for company for much of the game but he still ended with 26 disposals. He was one of just two players on the ground who didn't register a mark.
Despite the loss Smith still managed 30 disposals and 7 marks. His lowest since opening round but still a good score that we can't be unhappy with.

This makes it two in a row of 151 for Smith. He is having a stellar patch of form and with it his value keeps going up. 33 disposals 8 marks and 7 tackles for him. He may be out of reach at the moment.

Smith had his own footy early but then had the Robertson tag. This didn't completely stop his scoring though as he finished with 34 disposals and a goal. You need to find a way to bring him in if you don't have him.
Smith got off to a hot start and ended with 33 disposals to go with 14 contested possessions and 6 clearances to lead the Cats in those categories.
Baz went bang in the wet with a huge 40 touches and 10 tackles to simply dominate this game and post the second biggest score we have seen so far this year.
This was more like the Bailey Smith we were used to after that poor showing in opening round. He racked up 31 with a goal showing faith for those that selected him.
Smith didn't look the player he did last year. Not his best and even though this score won't be in his price cycle after his first movement he will drop.
Stewart is the key to the Cats. 7 marks and 28 disposals at 89% for the defensive star.  This was his second best score for the season.
Stewart had 21 touches in his 200th game as he did have Ned Long playing a bit of a forward tag on him.
This is now three under 65 in the last four for Tom which is a concern for owners. Just 14 disposals and 5 marks for him.
Stewart had 22 kicks to go with 5 handballs to be the best scorer for the Cats. His first over 100 in the last three.
This is now two quiet games in a row from Stewart which is a concern for those holding him. For those that don't have him his price should be very affordable shortly.
Very quiet day by Tom's standards with his first score under 110 for him this season and by a big distance. His price will drop for a couple of weeks with this in his cycle.
Stewart was the epitome of a loose man and was allowed to do as he pleased with 21 kicks 6 marks and 9 intercept possessions.
If it wasn't for the injury risk Stewart would have been in more teams. 10 marks for him to go with his 27 disposals. If he stays healthy he could be a play for us.
Stewart was one of the better scorers for the Cats but select with caution as we know he can miss through injury at any point.
Ash compiled 34 disposals at 67%. He hasn't been under the 90 mark for the last 4 games now.
Ash had the second most points for the Giants thanks to 9 marks and 23 disposals at 82%. He is one that we have had our eye on and this broke a run of three in a row under 100.

Ash dropped in his price as he didn't get to his big BE. It was his third below 100 in a row this week but it is two in the 90s in the last two. His BE at 122 means you can wait on him to bring him in.
30 disposals for Ash and while it was below 100 it wasn't by much. His BE has risen and as a result he will get cheaper. Be patient and we can get him cheap.
29 touches for Ash with 8 marks but just 4 contested and 1 clearance which led to his first under 100 since opening round. It was a tight game so don't worry about him.
Ash managed 35 disposals and 4 marks. This is four over 100 now in a row and it is making him a must have down back.
Ash is again putting up his hand as one of the players we must consider. He put out 28 disposals at 85% and took 10 marks and he did this with Whitfield having a big game too which is a great sign.
Ash has now posted back to back good scores and is showing that he is again one that we need to have in our sights for an upgrade during the year. 39 disposals and 9 marks.
Ash is off to a flyer with a great game in the big loss as the ball did spend a lot of time down his end.
Briggs was well beaten by English and spent just 51% of the game on the ground. This is a huge issue with Riccardi playing well around the ground.

Callaghan was one of 5 Giants over 100 with his 30 disposals and 6 clearances. This was the second time he has had back to back 100+ scores and he will be looking to do that again next week against the Eagles.
This was Finn's best score in the last three weeks. 28 disposals and 7 clearances was a good bounce back after a couple of quieter games.
Finn had 21 disposals but just 6 contested possessions and 1 tackle. It is now two poor scores in a row which is a big concern.

Callaghan was being tagged by Jordon but he still managed to rack up 26 disposals with a goal. But he was under pressure with just 46% efficiency and 9 clangers. The Jordan tag will hold most mids so don't panic.
Callaghan just dominated the game. 17 contested possessions 6 clearances and 37 disposals.  He is fast looking like a must have. A BE of 84 is more than achievable for him.

Callaghan was one of a number of Giants with more handballs than kicks but when you get 35 disposals at 82% that is not as big an issue. His scoring is certainly justifying his price and he is a valid option after this bye.
Callaghan managed 32 disposals but the efficiency of just 62% did hurt him. This is two in the 80s now which is a concern but we expect him to still score well going forward.
Callaghan really looks like taking the next step in the absence of Tom Green and justifies his selection being one of only two Giants over 100 in the heavy loss.
Had an interrupted preseason with a hip issue. He was well below his priced at figure in this game. Look for him to pick up as he gets a couple more games under his belt.
Cogs took a knock to the head and failed the HIA so will miss this week.
Cogs had a quiet one with his 13 disposals and 6 marks. This marks his lowest of the year and with a 60 in round one it shows us he won't be consistent so will be a risky own.
Coniglio is one that many overlooked this preseason as we were worried about his body but he was fantastic against the Hawks and needs to be considered.
Daniels got off to a quick start in the game but did slow down ending with a couple of goals from his 13 disposals.
This makes two games for Daniels now and both have been good with a great game this week. However we know he has a poor injury history so just beware if you take the risk.
Daniels returned to the side this week with 3 goals from his 14 disposals which is a solid result for him.
Fonti jumped back up again with a good score in the loss with the 17 disposals and goal. His BE is high but with the good bye it could be worth keeping him til then.
Fonti's scoring has been all over the place this season with a 91 last week and a 48 this week it makes him a hard one to own. He just got past his BE so he may be one we need to move on soon.
This was Joe's best score since opening round and it has bought him more time in our team with his BE dropping to 44.
15 touches for Fonty and his best in a few weeks. He beat his BE but with a new one of 73 it may be time to have him in your trade plans particularly as he is suspended for this week.
Fonti hit his BE but it was also his lowest score of the season so far. So his BE is now 78 so just watch him as he may have run out of cash gen for you.
Fonti delivered again with 10 marks and 21 disposals. The opportunity to use him as a cash cow has pretty much disappeared though with a BE of 57 now.
Fonti continued his good form to start the season and managed 16 disposals with 6 marks. Those that jumped aboard have been well rewarded
Fonti has had a couple of great games now and if you have an underperforming rookie it could be worth a swap to him before his price rise
Time to go for Phoenix as this was his second in the 40s in a row and his last four have been under 60.
Gothard is now missing his BE and his value is going to start to drop. He is a must trade.
This is two in a row in the 50s now for Gothard which was just above his BE but that has now risen to 97 which means he must be on your list to trade out soon.
After his two best for the season we saw Gothard have just the 10 disposals and it was the goal that helped him. He has two big scores dropping out so his BE is up to 39 now.

Gothard couldn't back up last weeks score but was still good and justified the selection of those that took him. 19 touches but 14 were by hand. Just keep a watch on him and be ready to trade out in the coming weeks.
Two goals for Gothard this week boosted that scoring from the two in the 40s we had seen early on. We really need to see another like this before we look at doing anything towards bringing him in.
Solid debut with a late goal but not one we are high on this year.
An ACL injury will see Green miss the entirety of the 2026 season
3 free kicks against for Toby and his lowest score for the season.
Greene was everywhere and had 29 disposals but the efficiency was the problem with 55% which did hold his score back.

4 free kicks against for Greene isn't what we want to see as we know he can have this problem.
This was about what we expect from Toby. He could be one we look at up forward but don't expect big scores each week.
Clarry racked up 38 disposals and he led the game in both contested possessions and clearances with 24 and 12 respectively.
6 kicks with 30 handballs and 7 tackles. But he did give away 3 free kicks. This was just his second score under 100 and the first since round 1.
Clarry was fantastic with 32 disposals and a game high 9 clearances and equal game high 13 contested possessions. Still just the one score under 100 for him this season.
Clarry remains consistent and is scoring well. This is heading back to where Clarry was one of the best in the league. He has only had the one sub 100 game.
Oliver has really settled in to the Giants midfield. 18 contested possessions 9 clearances to go with 37 disposals.
Oliver had the 31 disposals and it makes it 4 over 100 from his five games now. He is really slotting into that Giants midfield now. Worth a look for you team.

Clarry was solid and has posted back to back 100+ for the first time this season but again the kick to handball ratio was 11 to 26 which can limit his scoring. However the game high 16 contested possessions and 9 clearances certainly outweighs that.
This is what we get from Oliver. Some up and down in his scoring. And this week represented what we were used to which was 9 kicks and 24 handballs.
Clarry was quiet for his second game in Giants colours but the team were well beaten so don't panic on him.
Clarry slotted in nicely at the Giants with a game high clearance tally in the game. Many weren't sure of how he would go but he was amongst the best on the ground.
Solid first game with a goal and his 13 disposals. As always wait for another week to see what he does.
Riccardi is being used as a ruck more around the ground by the Giants with the new rules really helping him.
Unfortunately Rowston wasn't the starting  pick that we had hoped for. Time to move away from him if you are still holding.
Rowston was a popular name in the preseason and after a second lower score now he needs to be traded out before his price moves in his next game.
Rowston has been talked about in recent weeks. He is a beneficiary of a number of key Giants missing so he could only get a short run of a good role. Be ready to pull the trigger when others return
Whitfield was tagged by Murdock this week and really struggled early before making his way to 21 disposals at 85%. His lowest since opening round.
Whitfield was under a cloud after leaving training early during the week but he looked fine with a huge game including 26 kicks 9 handballs and 7 marks. His best score this season.
Whitfield was the best for the Giants with his 30 disposals coming at 80%. He is one of the ones you should be targeting as he has the good bye.
Whitfield was the best scorer for the Giants and he has been on quite a run over the last four games. If you are shopping for a defender he is certainly one to consider.
29 touches at 80% for Whitfield. His third over 100 in a row and he is really starting to hit some great form. One you must consider for your side.
Whitfield had 31 disposals at 87% and he looks strong again this season and will be right up there as someone to look at as we move into upgrades.
Whitfield was the top scoring Giant thanks to 39 disposals at 87%. With Ash also scoring well it shows us that they can both have big games together which is a good sign.
Whitfield finished with the 28 disposals. An improvement on last week for him and he isn't one to worry about at the moment as his price will continue to reduce for now.
Whitfield got plenty of the footy on the outside with just 3 of his disposals being contested. Don't panic trade him as this should be an anomaly for him and the Giants.
For those considering Whitfield he didn't do anything to tell us we shouldn't pick him.
First game for Dalton with 10 disposals. Nothing here that tells us that we can rely on him for scoring.
Day will be missing for much of the season with a shoulder injury.
Gunston booted 5 from 8 kicks this week. He did as he pleased but don't expect this each week.
Macdonlad struggled to put up a big score from his 21 disposals and goal.  He has been over 80 just twice in the last 5 games.
Only 12 disposals for Macdonald which is well down on what we want. His disposal efficiency was also below 70%. This was his lowest for the season and also his second under 60 in the last four.
Macdonald was the top scorer for the Hawks with 3 goals from his 28 disposals. He has been a little up and down so hopefully this will spark him going forward.
We know he can score but unfortunately it has been too inconsistent for us. If he could make this score his floor then he would need to be in every team.
Not the game Macdonald owners were hoping for. 15 disposals at just 53% efficiency with 7 clangers. He was playing off half forward which can be a bit of a dead spot for fantasy scoring.
Macdonald backed up his good outing in round 4 with 23 disposals and a goal.
Macdonald was the top scoring Hawk with his best score of the season so far. 26 disposals for him this week. This is like what we expected from him during preseason. A great game.

This was a much lower return for Macdonald after his first two good games. Still a good price rise coming for him. He did seem to have that role we didn't want for him which was that half forward one.

Macdonald was in and out of sides all preseason and the talk that he may not get the midfield time we wanted saw him end in 6% of teams. His score may have been inflated as the Hawks dominated the game but he still only attended 24% CBAs after 33% last week.
Macdonald did spend some time in the midfield which is what we want to see. His score was good in a game where the Hawks were well beaten. He had 12 CBAs which was well behind Newcombe's 32
First game for McCabe with 4 marks and 6 disposals plus a goal. We will need to see more from him in game two before we jump aboard.
Great kick after the siren for Moore to tie the game but he had just 1 contested possession to go with his 18 disposals. This was his second poor score in a row.
More will be missing this week through suspension.
Moore was great with 3 goals from 22 disposals. He has found his rhythm after a very quiet opening round game. He has dropped in price but there are probably still better options.
24 disposals and a good role for Moore in the big win. Don't jump on just yet. Let's see one more against a stronger opposition.
Moore didn't show anything that would make us want to select him.
Newcombe was well held in the second term but was good after half time with his 24 disposals including 12 contested possessions which was the most for the Hawks.
Newcombe just missed his fifth 100+ score in a row from his 26 disposals. He did attend the equal most centre ball ups for the Hawks with 22. Nothing to be concerned about.
Newcombe's ton run kept going this week thanks to his 28 disposals. He started to get going in that midfield this week as he had the most CBAs for the Hawks
Newcombe continues to be amongst the best for the Hawks. 30 disposals with 20 contested possessions and 12 clearances which led the game in both categories.
Newcombe was best for the Hawks thanks to his 7 tackles and 24 disposals. He has been over 100 four times now and this week was the first time this season he didn't have the most CBAs for the Hawks.
Newcombe was back above 100 with this being his best of the season so far. 28 disposals and a goal to go with a huge 14 clearances.
Newcombe was a little off this week. However he led the Hawks with 14 contested possessions and 6 clearances.
31 disposals for Newcombe as his last couple of games have been more of what we would like. A bye this week before you consider if you want him.
Newcombe was good in the middle for the Hawks with 22 touches. The Hawks had things easy as they dominated the game.
Newcombe led the CBAs for the Hawks with 32 but like many of the Hawks he couldn't convert that into points for us.  Pass for now.
Reeves had a poor night despite 24 disposals Just 5 disposals.
First game for Ryan and just 27 points from 7 disposals. He isn't one we have on our radar to bring in.
This was back to back over 100 for Sicily for the first time since the first two games of the season. 23 disposals and 8 marks for the Hawks defender.

Sicily had a good battle with the Docker forward and he had 22 disposals of which 20 were effective and he also had 10 marks. After being under an injury cloud it was good to see a solid score from him.
Sicily was struggling with an ankle issue late in the game and is questionable for this week and possibly the one after.
Sicily had 17 touches and his lowest of the year but he has also been suspended for 1 week for a punch.
Sicily was better this week after a couple of sub 100 scores. He took 13 marks which led the game in that category. He looks to be putting together a very solid start to the season.
Despite this being his lowest this year he has gotten off to a great start this season. This is vintage Sicily and he is putting his name up for us to consider again.
Sicily was great down back taking 11 marks. He isn't one that we need to jump on though.
Sicily tried to lift his team after half time. And it showed as he was the top scoring Hawk by over 30 points! We weren't talking about him but maybe we should be.
Watson kicked 3 goals but had just 9 disposals at 66%. He isn't a big possession getter and this was his lowest score of the season.
3 goals for Watson from just 11 disposals as he was flashing in and out of the game. His scoring hasn't gone over 80 though since round 4
2 goals from his 15 disposals. Not a big night for him but his scoring hasn't been as good as we would like.
Just 2 goals from 14 disposals for Watson this week. This is around the mark of scoring that we would expect.
Watson had 4 goals and 17 disposals. He was allowed to run around as he pleased against the Bombers. Don't expect this level of freedom from him regularly.

Gawn was once again the best Demon on the park with an equal high in Contested possessions and clearances for the game.  Heath did go off with a  head knock but did return so Gawn spent a bit more time in ruck than expected.

Gawn dominated the ruck as we expected this week racking up 21 disposals and a goal to go with 14 contested possessions but he did attend just over 50% of ruck contests. He is still yet to go under 100 this season.
Gawn spent much of the game up forward as they let Heath ruck against Grundy. Despite that Max still scored a ton and had 18 disposals and 22 hit outs. But hasn't been over 110 in the last three now.
Max kept his scoring run over 100 going but only just. He is dropping in value and will be a cheap pick up soon with a BE of 189 this week.

Max remains over 100 this week with his 21 disposals and 23 hit outs. It was the 15 contested possessions and 7 clearances that boosted his score. He isn't at the top of his scoring so he can go bigger from here.

Gawn was heavily traded in and with good reason. He managed 19 contested possessions amongst his 22 disposals and 11 clearances. A great all round game against the inexperienced Essendon rucks. A must have this season.
Gawn. There isn't much more we can say about him with another dominant performance this time over Witts. He is now the must have ruck in SuperCoach. 22 disposals a goal and 16 contested possessions.
Huge game for Max with 58 hitouts. He has shown us that he is certainly not being hurt by the new rules. He is now looking to be the R1 we must have for the season.
Gawn again was the best scorer for the Demons thanks to his 7 clearances and 15 contested possessions while he took 11 marks. He is showing the new rules aren't impacting his scoring ability.
Gawn had no issues dealing with TDK and the new rules to be the top scoring Demon in the game. Very safe to keep playing as your R1.
Langford had a huge week by his standards. A good week for owners but we want to see another game like this before we jump on.
Lindsay has posted two solid scores now and is likely to rise nicely after his third game.

Pickett copped the tag from Maginness and it hurt him with just 13 disposals but it was the 2 goals that did help his scoring. This is now two sub 100 in a row for the first time since the opening two rounds of the season.
Pickett had a tag from Hough after half time and he had his lowest for the season. He escaped suspension for the incident with Waterman and should be fine this week.
Pickett got the Jordon tag as expected but he still managed a couple of goals from 22 disposals and he led the team with 8 clearances.
Pickett was outstanding with 4 goals the result of 27 kicks and 2 handballs. He has been a popular trade in over recent weeks and will be one of the top two or three forwards.

Kossie has been a popular trade in over recent weeks and this week he delivered again. He is definitely a good option for your forward line but his BE is over 120 however he is up against Richmond so could hit that score.
8 tackles and 2 goals to go with his 28 disposals for Pickett. Despite not reaching 100 due to 3 free kicks against he was still the third highest scorer for his team.
Kossie Pickett was great again in the second half helping to set up the win for the Dees. He should be high on our list of trade ins for the forward line the way he is going.

Kossie Pickett really pulled one out of the bag and was the catalyst for the Demons comeback with his 33 disposals and 7 marks. His score was elevated by the fact he helped to turn the tide of the game.
Pickett has had a low score again this week and is likely to drop in value after his third round.
Latrelle had an efficiency of just 53% and another low score. He is one to trade out.
Latrelle had his second lowest score and with this is losing value. He is a must trade out.
Quiet game from just 59% TOG for Latrelle as he slotted a goal from his 7 disposals.
Salem left the game with an ankle injury so time to trade if you have him.

Steele topped the game in contested possessions with 14 to go with his 26 disposals and was able to post his best in the last three weeks. He has slowed in scoring but he won't be your biggest issue this week.
21 of his 26 disposals were handballs this week at 69%. This was his second under 90 in a row and three of the last four under 100 which is a concern.
This was Steele's lowest for the season. Just 4 of his 19 were kicks. He saved his score with 11 contested possessions and 6 clearances. He won't be your biggest concern.
Steele just keeps delivering with 25 disposals this week at 80%. His scoring is consistent and that is all we can ask for.
Steele was 1 point shy of his 100 last week. He is still consistently scoring and is not one of your concerns.
Many had Steele as a VC or C but with the Bombers winning we didn't see a huge score from Jack. 28 disposals for him to be one of just two Dees with 100 or more.
Steele is continuing to show some great form with his 26 disposals and 8 tackles. Nothing to worry about with him as he led the game in both Contested possessions and clearances.
Steele hasn't let us down yet despite what some people have said. His game included an impressive 16 tackles!
Steele was better this week and showed us what he is capable of as one of just three Demons to hit the 100.  9 tackles were the key for Jack along with his 31 disposals. Hold for now.
Steele gave us pretty much what we expected which was the third highest for the Dees this week. 21 disposals and a goal. However he did look slow which is a concern. He won't be a long term play.

Windsor had an ankle issue early but played out the game with 22 disposals and 4 clearances. It is back to back in the 80s for him but his BE has risen with that 102 dropping out of his cycle.

Those that stuck with Windsor were well rewarded with his best score of the season from his 25 disposals and 2 goals. Temper this though as they don't play Richmond every week.
Windsor continues to drop in value after this week's 12 disposals. His new BE is up at 77. He should be a priority trade out after he had 17 CBA's which is more than his touches.
Windsor struggled this week with just 7 disposals. His lowest score which has now seen him drop in value. He should be on your list to upgrade as soon as you can.

7 tackles and 17 disposals for Windsor but his efficiency was not great at just 52%. He made his BE but he is looking to be one of the next on the block for us as we look to start upgrading our sides from here.
Windsor was better this week and posted his equal best score for the season. He isn't smashing it but he is also scoring ok and is making money.
A bit of a step down in scoring from Windsor this week. The Demons battled all game which didn't help. Just the 13 disposals. A BE of 40 means that he won't be the cash generator we hoped.
Popular selection Windsor started in the middle and was very serviceable for us with 21 disposals and a goal. You are going to have bigger issues than Windsor to deal with this week.
A good preseason from Windsor who looks to have won a spot in the midfield for the Demons

LDU is yet to drop below 110 this season and is really putting his hand up as a potential great lowly owned pick for you this year.

LDU continued his great start to the season and is lowly owned at just 6.5% so he is a handy own for those that have him.
LDU racked up again this week with his 23 disposals. He is having a good start to the season and he could be in the mix for us.
LDU had a couple of really good patches in the game and is showing some great form. A good 24 disposals.

Just 10 touches for Dovaston. He beat his BE but not by much. He has been under 50 for his last three now. Time to move him.
