Dovaston posted his lowest of the year and whilst he made his BE which was negative it has now risen to 13 which means he may be a really short burn for us.
Dovaston was in the 40s again this week. Not big scoring but with other issues he is doing enough to not lose money.
Dovaston was ok but not huge. 10 disposals and looked ok. He looks locked into that side.
19 touches but it was his lowest in the last three for Colby in what was an ordinary day for the Roos. This high half forward role doesn't look like changing. Move him on if you can.
Colby had that half forward role but did have 25 disposals at 88%. Three over 80 now in the last three. This score was more towards where we want him to be.
The role change is real but this week he showed he can score from it with 2 goals the result of his 23 disposals. He dropped in value but it was a better return than his last three games.
Red Alert. Colby looks to have had a real role change now and is up forward more which is not the role we brought him in for. 17 disposals but importantly this was his lowest score since round 1.

A bit of a red alert this week with Colby spending time up forward which is a concern for owners. We prefer him in that half back role where he can score more. He did have 26 touches but if that role persists he could drop.
McKercher had a good first half but did slow a little after that. His lowest score since round 1.
Colby was talked about everywhere to get traded in and he certainly paid dividends for those that did.  Despite a quiet third term he put in a great game for new owners with 24 disposals at 83%.
This is certainly the role and scoring we wanted to see from Colby when he was one of the hype players in pre season. 35 disposals from him and this score has seen his BE land at 67s.
When Griffin Logue went down we saw more of Colby off the half back which is the role we want. 20 disposals at 85%. If Logue is out for a while Colby should benefit.

After plenty of concerns as to whether McKercher was going to play he lined up and he did struggle to score so hopefully this is just a one off. We have another week before his price moves so you can hold.
A fractured finger in the preseason has seen Coby have surgery but is still looking set for round 1
Finn's second best score this year and best since he returned to the team. 22 disposals and a couple of goals as he had the job of tagging Heeney for much of the game.
Parker top scored for the Roos with his 28 disposals also being the equal highest in the game. It was an awful day for the Roos but it was his best score in the last three.
10 marks for Parker and 24 of his 29 disposals were by foot. A great bounce back form last week's poor score.
Parker bounced back to the form of round 1 with a. massive score from 33 disposals and 13 marks. But remember he won't play Essendon ever week.
Parker was the star for the Roos and spent time down back but did move to the mids at times.
Sheezel had his third sub 100 in the last four an it was also his lowest of the season. The Roos were never really in the contest which really hurt his score.
Sheezel got his first over 100 for the last three weeks.31 disposals and a goal and a game high 7 tackles.
Sheezel got the tag from Mullin but he still managed his 20 disposals and goal. This was his lowest for the year however and is now two under 100 in a row. Look for him to bounce back next week.
We were worried with his finger injury but he played and it didn't impact him too much with 32 disposals and a goal.
Sheezel did Sheezel things with another massive score. 39 disposals to go with 8 marks and 7 clearances. He is a VC or C option for you every week.
30 disposals this week for Sheezel with another 120+ score. Great bounce back after last week. Always an option for your C or VC.
Sheezel didn't put up a huge score like many thought he might with his 24 disposals and a goal. He made the BE this week but his price will start to drop so non owners keep a watch on him.
Sheezel again went big and is a perma captain option for us this season. 11 marks and 33 disposals at 87% is fantastic in any language.
Sheezel was on a hot pace but that did slow when the Eagles got going. However nothing to worry about with his 40 disposal 8 clearance game.
Sheezel spent time floating between half back and midfield during the game and he scored big as he was allowed to do as he wanted. If you didn't start him look to get him in.
Stephens scores have been too up and down for us to consider him a solid own. His value went up this week but he won't move a great deal more with scores like this.
This was his lowest so far and it would appear that if you brought him in he may have run out of steam.
Stephens showed glimpses of what we saw in round 1. He is still likely to be a bit inconsistent to be in our sides.
Stephens has now shown us that the score in R1 was a once off so now he isn't one that we want .
Stephens was good but not up to that level of his first game which is not unexpected. He did manage 70 points but he isn't one that we should rush into our team.
Stephens was the real surprise packet for the Roos with a big game. Just keep an eye on him for one more week before you make a move to get him in.
Back to back in the 90s is making us sit up and have a look at Trembath. But don't go making any moves to get him in unless you think he can continue with this form.
Wardlaw laid 11 tackles to lead the game and was better this week. Don't jump on him on the back of this one performance though.
Wardlaw came back into the side this week and didn't do enough to interest us in picking him.
Xerri battled with McAndrew but ultimately had his second worse score this year. His tackle count was well down at just 2 as North were well beaten all over the ground.
Xerri won the battle with Grundy despite losing the hit out count. He was more dominant around the ground with 9 clearances and 19 disposals.
Xerri was massive as he topped last week's big score. 26 contested disposals and 14 clearances to go with 30 disposals. He was unstoppable against the undermanned Cats rucks.
Xerri came back in and made up for lost time as he led the game in tackles contested possessions and clearances. He is one that we need to target.

Xerri was a popular trade in but had a horrible score with 3 free kicks against and 15 disposals. However he will be suspended after wiping blood on McGrath. He is now missing for 3 weeks so you could trade him.

Xerri went to another level against Flynn and was just short of the 200 mark with 43 hitouts and 23 contested possessions amongst his 25 disposals and 9 tackles. Any thoughts he was going to struggle with the new rules are being put to bed.
Xerri dominated around the ground against the younger Power ruckman but he didn't have a hit out in the first quarter but did get  his 10 tackles to lead the game in that category.
First game for Tom and he was ok with 16 disposals. It wasn't enough to go early on him but we may be in need of a rookie soon.
Bergman left the game with a toe injury that now requires surgery and there is no timeline on a return but at best it wouldn't be until after their R12 bye.
A goal boosted Bergman's score but he isn't putting up the scoring you need to have him on your field.
Bergman had his best for the year but he still isn't showing us enough to say he should be in our SuperCoach teams.
Bergman still doesn't look right and he isn't an option for us at the moment.
Bergman left the game with an ankle injury in the third term but did return however his scoring isn't at the level we need. You can't hold him.
Bergman was in the midfield but Port got smashed in the centre square an this limited his scoring. He was on limited minutes as he still recovers from that foot injury.

Brodie played his first game for the Power in the midfield and got 28% CBA. He had 4 kicks and 14 handballs. Job security isn't fully there with Wines collecting over 30 disposals in the SANFL. Wait another week at least.

Butters was trying to carry the Power over the line with 35 disposals and he led the team in contested possessions and had the game equal high clearances. He is a machine and delivering exactly what we expected. A must have.
Butters was the highlight for the Power with 30 disposals and 5 clearances. This was his best in the last three and 5th score over 120.
Butters kept that ton run going with 30 disposals and 6 tackles. A huge second quarter after a 7 point first term.
Butters fought through the Bullin tag well as the Power took control of the game. He ended with 30 disposals but did give away 5 free kicks.

Butters was electric after quarter time as he led the game with 16 contested possessions and 35 disposals. He is up against Osin Mullin this week who held him to two scores under 50 last season though.
Butters was the best for the Power with 31 disposals and 16 contested possessions. He posted his best score of the season in the wet. He was found guilty of umpire abuse but will not miss a game.
Butters was very quiet in the first half but came to life after half time and was the impetus for the Power running away with the game in that second half. 30 disposals and a team high 6 clearances.
Butters had a tag from Robertson but still managed 30 disposals. With no Rozee in the side there will be added attention to Butters each week.
Butters was outstanding as there was no tag for him this week. 36 disposals and 7 marks. This is what we brought him in for and with the Eagles this week he will be looking to back this up.
Butters didn't take a mark and didn't use the footy well with his 23 disposals. Not his day as he just struggled to find space as he was tagged by O'Sullivan.
Mitch could have kicked 9 goals but was inaccurate with 4.6 on the night.

JHF had the footy 17 times but an efficiency of just 47% really hurt him as he continues to leak cash and see his BE rise. He isn't scoring enough to be in your plans but if he is you should be waiting until after his bye at least.
JHF had the 18 disposals and 15 were effective however his score was still his second lowest for the year and worryingly it was his second in the 70s for the last two weeks.
JHF had a great start to the game but did slow in the second half with his 20 disposals and 7 clearances which was the equal highest in the game. Not a big score so you can hold off on him.
JHF had his own footy at times with his 34 disposals and he had a huge 12 clearances. This is now two of 110+ in a row. Time to jump aboard if you want him. Just beware of that r12 bye.
Horne-Francis had his first over 100 since round 2 and also beat his BE. He racked up 2 goals from 28 disposals and 7 marks. With his forward status we will need to consider him.
26 disposals for JHF with a couple of goals. Again free kicks against were an issue with 3. He isn't scoring well enough for us to need to bring him in though.
Horne-Francis really only got into the game when he went up forward which is good for his DPP chances but his scoring isn't at a level that we would like to see.

JHF didn't have the score we were hoping for and was around half of last week's performance. He did spend a bit of time up forward but did have 66% CBA so we are just going to have to accept inconsistent scoring from him.
This is the JHF that we all know can take on a game. Three early goals with 10 marks and 26 disposals as he took the game on and set up the win early. We need to see more of this from him more often.
JHF copped the ire of the Roos fans and he didn't have a great game with just 12 disposals. He is one to stay away from for now.
Lai had his lowest score and he now has a BE of 28 which isn't what we want to see.
Lai played his second game and whilst he had a decent enough score he isn't going to play Richmond each week.
Lai's first game wasn't outstanding but he was serviceable. Don't jump aboard though as we need to see another game.
Lukosius is going to miss a number of weeks so if you are holding you need to trade.
Marshall was dropped and it could be the start of a longer term spell in the SANFL.
Marshall barely saw the footy in the first half and moved between forward and back during the game.
Another solid game from Marshall with 10 intercepts. He didn't play forward with Lukosius out like we feared which means he is good to go for us still.
Marshall finished with 13 disposals. He spent the last quarter and a half  up forward in his familiar role. He is still making money and has a new BE of -1.
Marshall missed the game after rolling his ankle again at training. He is expected to be ok this week to go ahead so just watch the team sheets.
Marshall was the link player across half back with 11 marks and 15 kicks and 0 handballs. His BE of -78 will see him a very popular trade in before his price moves this week.

Marshall was looking good with some intercept possessions and a great efficiency but did hurt his ankle in the last quarter and was iced up before the end of the game. Scans came back ok and he should play this week.

Rozee looked good until he hyper extended his leg in the third term and didn't return to the game and is now looking at a significant stint on the sidelines with tendon damage to the hamstring. A must trade.
Rozee was the only Power player over 100 and he did spend a lot more time in the midfield than we expected. Don't move him on as he should get better as the team improve.
Sweet found it tough against Moyle and Witts as well as the slippery conditions in Darwin and posted his lowest score this season.
Sweet did a good job against English but his disposals were down at 10 as he finished with his second lowest score this year.
Sweet had a big outing against McAndrew and had 14 contested possessions and 5 clearances.
Sweet top scored in the game with 31 hitouts and 12 disposals. He had it his own way with the two Cats rucks getting injured in the game.
Sweet was the second best scoring Power player as he had a good night in the ruck against TDK and RoMar. He won the hitouts along with having 12 contested possessions and 5 clearances.
Sweet posted a big score but don't get excited as he didn't have a great deal of opposition from Samson Ryan.
Sweet came back into the side and outmuscled Blakiston. This game should keep Visentini out for a while.
We've seen two games from Dante in a row now and this one was much better with 22 hitouts and 10 disposals but the Cats lost both rucks early in the game which helped.
Visentini was recalled to the side this week but didn't show us enough. Just 2 disposals 4 tackles and 14 hitouts. We can't hold him.

Dante was outmuscled by Xerri around the ground but did ok in the centre bounces. 30 hitouts was good to go with 6 tackles. He is going to be undersized against a lot of rucks so don't expect a lot more.
Watkins held his spot this week and thanks to a very low BE he rose in value from his 11 disposals. But a new BE of 12 means you can hold him for one more week and then he has his bye in R12
Watkins came back into the side this week and it was a better score than his previous game with a goal and 13 disposals. However he is still one to trade out.
Watkins was a late in for Marshall and had just 34% time on ground for 6 disposals. He hasn't scored over 25 now in his last three games.
Watkins was dropped after a couple of poor games.
Watkins had just the 17 points this week after 7 the prior week and is losing money. He is a must trade as soon as possible with a high BE. His efficiency was just 30% in the wet.

Watkins was cold as ice with just 8 disposals and only 3 of them being effective in 64% time on ground. After going in with a -51 BE he comes out with a 33 BE but with tougher teams to come are we seeing the end of him as a cash cow?

Watkins didn't get the boost in CBA that we expected with 31% after 59% the week before with Will Brodie taking the remainder of his share. No concerns with his scoring overall so you can hold him still this week.
Watkins was good again this week and with Rozee's injury he is now likely to stay in the side even with Wines returning this week.
Good debut for Watkins with 10 disposals. The Power were awful which didn't help him get any free footy anywhere. The risk for him is when Wines is back in round 3 and does he hold his spot.
Wines is missing through suspension until round 3.
Banks suffered a broken collarbone and will miss a number of weeks.
Banks wasn't a highly owned and was priced in the 80s and that is the range he scored in. But a pass for now.
Cumming had just 13 disposals as he made his BE but his new one is 63 which is rising faster than we had hoped. He is one you can trade out.
Cumming couldn't back up his great start to his career as he was held to just 8 disposals this week. He went at 87% but his BE has now risen sharply to 17.
Cumming's second game netted 23 points and 6 tackles. He will be an incredibly popular trade in this week.
Cumming showed on debut that he is every bit the scorer we thought he was going to be with 5 clearances and 8 contested possessions with his 13 touches. Give him one more week before bringing him in.
Cumming will out til round 5 at least with a shoulder injury
Grlj returned this week and missed his BE from his 17 disposals. He is one we should look to move on.
Grlj was a late out this week.
Sam had only 9 disposals and just made it to his BE. Time to move him on with his BE now up over 70.
Grlj finished with 21 disposals and beat his BE. His new BE of 43 though means he is one you can trade out.
Grlj put up 16 disposals. His BE has risen to 53 with the 90 about to drop from his cycle. He should still be good to go one more week as he shouldn't lose too much.
Second lowest for Sam so far this year but his BE remains low at 14 and with that we can certainly hold him for a little longer.

Grlj posted his best of the season this week from 19 disposals. With his lowest of the year rolling out of his average this week his BE is low at -13 meaning he will be making money for a few more weeks yet if he can hold his average.
Grlj ended with 18 disposals but just 61% efficiency.  This was better than his last game and it has got his cash generation going again.
Grlj didn't have the impact we saw from round 1 and this is going to happen with rookies so don't panic. He will still rise in value with his BE remaining low.
Grlj was the story of the game with his 19 disposals and 7 marks with a great debut. He is highly owned and with good reason. If you don't have him you may want to make plans to get him in.
First game for Hayes-Brown as the Tigers were running out of rucks. An ok first game but once some of the others come back he will be gone from the side.
Hopper just couldn't get going and he doesn't look to be an option for us despite 18 disposals.
Lalor kicked a goal from his 16 disposals. His scoring has been very consistent this season.
Lalor cracked his first ton of the season from 22 touches 6 marks and a goal thanks to great efficiency of 95%.
Lalor is yet to drop below 70. He is putting together a good start to the year and is still making some cash for us.
2 goals helped to boost Lalor's scoring this week as he had just the 12 disposals. His BE is still lower than his average but he doesn't look to be a keeper nor a cash cow.

Lalor posted his best for the year but 4 free kicks against didn't really help him. He isn't really a play for us as he isn't scoring enough and he now has a BE of 34 so won't make a heap of money either.
A second score in the mid 70s now for Lalor.  Whilst he is doing a great job for the Tigers he isn't one that we should be considering for our SuperCoach sides.
Lalor was good in bursts for the Tigers but only managed the 16 disposals. He scored enough to beat his price but not enough to be a big cash generator.
Miller has had back to back scores over 100 and is very lowly owned at the moment. His BE is very low and took 15 marks this week.

Solid game from Retschko despite being his lowest for the year. He isn't dominating but is doing enough for us to rise in value. If we can get a bit more from him and see him keep his spot in the byes that would be great.
Retschko was great for owners with his 22 disposals at 81%. This saw his BE remain low at 9 and a great pick. He is still going to make us some good money.
Retschko had the 9 touches and whilst his score wasn't as big as his first couple it was certainly ok for a cash cow. His BE remains very favourable so nothing to be concerned about.
Retschko was even better in his second game. He is a must trade in this week. He had 26 disposals and 6 contested possessions.

First game for Retschko and it was a good one with 6 marks and 13 disposals. He look like he could be a good downgrade but if you can wait let's see what happens next week in game two. With the Tigers injuries he should hold his spot.
Ross has put three in a row over 100 now with 23 disposals and 12 contested this week.
Ross was a down on last week. He hasn't been consistent of late. He isn't one that we can trust at the moment.
Ross had one out of the box this week with 26 disposals 2 goals as he also led the game in Contested possessions and clearances. His last three weeks have now been very solid.
Ross' scoring has been jumping up and down this season and this inconsistency is a little bit of a concern. We can't trust his scoring week to week which is so important in SuperCoach.
Ross put in another great score this week as many looked at him as a replacement for Petracca. 23 disposals for him and beat his BE nicely. One to watch.
Short top scored for the Tigers yet again this week with his 25 disposals and 7 marks and a 100% efficiency rating.
26 touches and 10 marks for Short as there was a lot of chipping across that back line at points. He went at 96% but just 4 contested touches.
Short was back in the side this week with 23 disposals and 6 marks. This is about what we should expect most weeks from him.
Short was a late out as his wife was in labour. He should return next week.

Short bounced back as he has been jumping around with his scoring over the last four games. He was up this week with 8 marks and 26 disposals. He has form from previous years so could be ok if we see a couple in a row.
This is now two in the 60s in the last three weeks for Short and this is something we can't be having from our players.
Short looks to have recaptured the form and role that we have seen from him in previous years a the playmaker. 19 kicks 3 handballs and 6 marks as he looks to be one we must consider.
Short really dropped off this week despite 10 marks and 20 disposals. Just 2 contested possessions and 75% efficiency.

Back to back 100+ scores to start the season for Short who took 13 marks and had 33 disposals. We stayed away due to his injury issues but he is making us consider him as he number 1 in the Tigers defence.
Short was the top scorer in the game with 10 marks to go with 23 kicks and 6 handballs. He did have some injury issues last year playing just 15 games. One to watch.
Taranto will miss this week with concussion after he had just 10 disposals and 45% time on ground this week.
Taranto isn't back to the form of his first season at Richmond but he has posted 4 over 100 in a row now as he is taking control of the Tigers midfield.
Taranto was the best for the Tigers and it marks three over 100 in a row for him with his biggest score this season with 10 tackles and 2 goals a part of his game.

As we have seen in the past Taranto got plenty of the footy but he just isn't one that we need to have in our sides. He scored well but the Tigers will struggle during the year which will limit his scoring.
Carroll showed some great form this week and beat his BE and sent it downwards with his 10 marks and 25 disposals at 84%. Great for us to keep him for a bit longer.

Carroll ended with 12 disposals and will have the 106 dropping out of his cycle after next week and hence his BE has now risen to 76 meaning he is one that we must look at trading as he has only beaten that score once this season..
Carroll couldn't replicate his big score from his previous week. With that 106 still in his price cycle his BE remains low at 0 so hold still.
Carroll had a huge game with 10 marks and 25 disposals. This has set his BE to 13 meaning with this score in his cycle we could keep him for a few weeks yet.
Carroll made his BE but not by much with his 11 disposals at 63%. His new BE of 21 means we could be in trouble and need to trade him in a week or two.
This was his best so far this year and it has sent his BE down to 5. This is a good result for those that held as he should be ok to be in our team for a few more weeks.

10 disposals for Carroll and it is now two in a row in the 40s for Jack. His BE has risen to 23. He doesn't look like a long term play so if you want to cash in on what we have made from him so far while on bye it isn't a bad plan
Carroll was a concern as to whether he would be dropped but he played and had 10 kicks and a handball. His BE of -11 is one that we can work with but not for a long time.

Carroll was brought into a lot of teams on the back of his AAMI and Opening round performances. But just 15 disposals for him didn't deliver a big score. His price will change after the next game so just take that into account.
Carroll is rookie priced but it was thought he could produce this season and more scores like this one he could be a great cash cow.

TDK had the sole ruck duties for most of the game with Marshall leaving the game with concussion. We don't really know what their true roles will be from that but TDK is probably still not a first choice for your ruck line.
Back to back over 100 for Flanders for the first time this year and it is exactly what owners were hoping for when we got him in. 28 disposals at 82% in the win.

Flanders top scored for the Saints with his 28 disposals and 7 marks. His best for the year and just his third over 100 but his scoring hasn't really been bouncing around which is great to have that consistency.
Flanders was disappointing with just 18 disposals with this being his lowest score of the season. We need him to be minimum 90.
Just the two over 100 this season from Flanders with a 21 disposal game this week. He isn't our biggest concern so hold for now.
Flanders isn't busting out huge scores but he is playing his role in our teams with 22 disposals this week and 6 tackles.
Flanders ended with no goals but had 23 disposals. Stick wit him. There were only a handful of big scores for the Saints in the win.
Flanders showed his worth with 28 disposals and this is what we wanted to see from him. This sort of score will see him a top 6 forward by season's end.
Marshall with three goals 9 marks and 22 disposals. He has put in three great weeks now as the Saints really look like they have got the two rucks working well together now.

Marshall spent the most time in ruck that he has all season with TDK getting injured early in the game. With that he had scoring like last year with 25 disposals 7 clearances and 22 hitouts. If TDK is out for a while he could be a good option.
Marshall continues to struggle to score in his new role and is now not someone that we can consider in Supercoach.
Marshall copped a knee to the back of the head resulting in concussion. He will miss round 1. We didn't get enough data to really see what he will do this year with just 50% of the game.
Phillipou started hot with a  couple of goals and ended with 17 disposals but did give away three free kicks unfortunately.
Phillipou had his second lowest score of the season with his 15 disposals and 9 marks.

20 disposals from Phillipou with this his first back to back good scores for the season. Not huge but it was better than we saw from him early in the season. Hopefully the start of something from him.
This is much more like what we all thought Phillipou could do. 2 goals from 18 disposals but remember it is against the Eagles who were poor. Hopefully he can push on from here.
Just 10 touches at 40% for Phillipou as he continues to be a let down for owners. His BE has risen to 37 and is unfieldable.
If you are still holding Phillipou then it is time to move on from him. We simply aren't seeing the scoring levels that we need.
Phillipou played despite the injury concerns but with just 2 kicks and 6 handballs. This was above his low BE but his new one of 38 means he simply isn't going to generate the cash we hoped.
Phillipou only made it through 43% time on ground before he exited with a corkie toward the end of the second quarter. Trade him if you started him.

Phillipou had the role we were after with plenty of CBAs however he didn't get the amount of possessions that we were looking for or the score we were looking for. He could be 50-50 for our starting teams with this level of scoring.
Sinclair had the second best score in the game from 21 kicks 8 handballs and 8 marks. This was his first back to back 100+ scores since before their early bye.
Sinclair had his first 100+ score in the last three weeks as he had to take a bit more of the footy with Wilkie going down. A goal and 25 touches for him this week.
Sinclair has had back to back in the 90s now and is  still a great option. He was very quiet in the second and  third but bounced back in the last to get that score going
It seems that Wiklie is doing some of what Sinclair also does. He still had 23 kicks and 4 handballs. Just his second sub 100 but they are both in the last three weeks.
Sinclair put up a 35 disposal game as he bounced back from last week's lowest of the season. He is a hugely popular selection and his BE of 143 means he will become more affordable after this week.
This was Sinclair's lowest of the year and first under 100. The role that was normally his was being done by Wilkie this week as that interceptor and distributor. Don't panic on him yet.

Sinclair was the best for the Saints. This is now over 110 for the four games this year. He is now one of the most needed defenders of the season. If you don't have him then plan to have him after this bye.
Sinclair had 31 disposals and used the footy well with a 90% efficiency. He is one that we need to get in at some stage.
Sinclair was again a star with his 31 disposals at 87% efficiency. He is one that we need to get into our side as soon as we can if you didn't start him.
Sinclair was the main man as there was some time put into Nasiah by the Pies.  We know Sinclair can flat out score and this was more evidence of it.  Worth a thought for you side.
Nas was a late out with a corked calf on the weekend and news has now emerged that he will miss a further three weeks with that injury.
Nas copped attention from Cowan but still had 31 disposals and a goal. He has a BE of 87 which is very achievable so if you do want him it would be a good time to bring him in.

NAS had Duursma for company early but it didn't have much impact as Nas did as he pleased after an early injury scare where he was winded. He beat his BE and has a new one of 121 so it is a good time to launch.

There were reports during the week that Nas wasn't quite right. He had Michaelanney as a tag for parts of the first and last term and despite having 28 disposals he had a game high 8 clangers and efficiency of just 67%.

Nas was the top scorer for the Saints with his two goals and 9 tackles that went along with his 28 disposals. He was tagged by Burgoyne for much of the game and is now starting to find his feet with the attention he now gets.

Nas was tagged again in the first half of this game but was released after half time. He recorded a season high 81% Centre ball up attendances and his second best score of the year. With more like this he will certainly be back on the radar after the slow start to the year.
This was more the Nas we are used to. 27 disposals and 5 clearances as the tag was dropped in the third term. We need to see him shake these tags more often.
Wanganeen-Milera was tagged again this week and again he was limited to 18 disposals with his score boosted from 3 goals while resting forward. His price will drop so you can wait to bring him in.
Wanganeen-Milera had Perryman tagging him and was held to just 19 possessions and a goal. He didn't get all the open footy that we saw last year.  This is a big red flag for those starting him.
Wilkie was able to play despite his sore back from last week and he put up a great score as he took 12 marks and his 25 disposals came at 92%.
Wilkie copped a knee to the back in the first term. He came back on but was taken out of the game at half time with just 5 disposals. Watch injury reports to see if he is good to go next week.
Whilst Wilkie's score was his first under 100 for the season he still took 12 marks and had 22 disposals. The ball wasn't in his area a great deal in the second half which didn't help his score.
Wilkie took a while to get going but he did and took 16 marks as he couldn't avoid the footy at times. 25 disposals at 96% efficiency led to yet another 100+ score.
Wilkie continues to be a star for the Saints with another 12 marks and 31 disposals this week. He hasn't been under 100 yet this season.
Wilkie hasn't dropped below 100 for the season so far and he needs to be someone that we consider going forward. He has a good role and these points should continue to flow.
Wilkie has had a great start to the season with his fourth score over 100 in his first four games. He is one that you have to seriously consider as he has a great role.
Wilkie was fantastic and has a great role down back as he had 11 marks and 28 disposals. Don't discount him in your plans for the season.
Wilkie has been a solid performer over the last few seasons and started well with a big possession game in opening round.
It looks like Windhager's first two games may have been an anomaly. He did have 19 disposals at a lowly 52% which was what hurt his score.
Windhager spent some time at half back and this was his first sub 100 for the season. He used the footy well but just didn't get the touches.
Windy racked up the disposals with 32 and an equal team high 6 clearances. He is certainly worth considering after his bye.
Big game for Bice to be the second highest scorer of the game.
Cootee played his second game and just the 11 disposals. He will be considered by many with a BE of 9 but his scoring won't see him generate much cash.
First game for Cootee and had 8 disposals with a goal. However his points weren't enough for us to jump early.
Curnow kicked just 1 goal from 9 disposals. He can't be relied upon unfortunately.
Cornow didn't touch it in the first quarter and kicked 1.4 from 8 disposals. He just isn't consistent enough to field
This is what the Swans bought Charlie for.  It was a bit of a soft kill for him against the depleted Dogs. We need to see this consistently from him before selecting him.
3 goals for Curnow this week but from just 10 disposals. He is still not fieldable for us unfortunately.
Despite 4 goals we didn't see a big score from Charlie. He isn't one you can bring in at this point.
Curnow really struggled this week despite 2 early goals. He barely saw the footy in the second half.

Grundy was simply outstanding as he posted the season's first 200+ score. 24 contested and 12 clearances to go with 34 disposals and 46 hit outs. The complete game from the star ruck against a very depleted Pies ruck division.

Grundy won the hit outs with 27 and 13 of them were to advantage. But around the ground he had just the 14 touches and 6 were effective. Xerri is always a tough opponent and this score is nothing to worry about .
Grundy top scored for the Swans in his 250th with 11 clearances 15 contested possessions 45 hit outs and 26 disposals. He did it all for his 6th of 120 or more in a row.
Grundy was huge against a Dogs ruck on his debut. He really put the foot down after half time to have his 2 goals and 18 disposals. This is now five in a row over 120.
Grundy was outstanding again with 27 disposals and 6 tackles. He now hasn't been under 120 since round 1. He is a constant C or VC option.
Grundy was one of the popular replacements for English this week. He won the contest with Witts comfortably with 36 hitouts 12 tackles and 20 disposals. Alongside Gawn is a must have ruck.

Grundy was massive against Flynn which seems to be a trend this year. 28 disposals 33 hitouts 18 contested possessions and 9 clearances to lead the game in all of those categories.  A huge performance.

Grundy really bounced back after last week to have a huge game against the Hawks pair. 19 disposals and a goal for him as he also led the Swans in clearances with 7. All the concern last week has been put aside.
Quieter from Grundy this week with just 2 kicks and 7 handballs along with 4 free kicks against.  Don't panic on him just yet as he did take a big hit during the game which hurt him.
We were unsure at half time but a big second half from Grundy saw him show that he is one we must consider as our R1. He faced stiff opposition and really lifted after a quiet first half.
Gulden was having a great game before he injured his shoulder in the last term. He is going to miss for 4 months so a must trade.
Gulden was at the top of a lot of shopping lists and this just cemented that. He was the one that really got the Swans going after half time.
Heeney had 20 contested disposals and 11 clearances to be second in both categories for the game to Grundy. This was his first under 100 since round 1 but there wasn't much in it!
Heeney was one of just two Swans to crack triple figures this week with 15 contested possessions 7 clearances and 3 goals.
Heeney had a great game with 33 disposals of which 22 were by hand. He has been on a great run in his last four games.
Heeney missed the game with some calf soreness and it is hoped he will return this week.
28 disposals for Heeney in the win making it three over 100 in a row now for him. He is always an option for us . If he does get forward status he will be a must own.

Heeney was the star of the game and did it all leading the game in clearances contested possessions and disposals. Don't expect this every week but with a very low BE this would be the time to get him in.
Heeney's return to the team was a fantastic one with 4 goals from his 26 disposals and 8 marks. He beat his BE and now has one of 98. Heeney is always one we need to be aware of as a possible target
Heeney left the game in the last quarter with a hamstring issue. He is likely to miss this week with the short turn around to Thurs night however is expected to return for the following game.
Heeney looks to have a similar role and one that will see some big scores but he will often deliver these just short of 100.
McInerney continued his great form this year with 31 disposals and a goal. This was his second best for the year and fourth over 100. A 50 point last term certainly didn't hurt.
This was the lowest score for the season for McInerney with just 7 of his 22 disposals were kicks and his efficiency was held to 63%.
29 touches for Justin with his first over 100 in the last four.
McInerney dropped back to the pack this week with 24 disposals after his great run to start the season. Just his second score under 90 for the season.
McInerney has had a very consistent first 6 games. 2 goals and 26 disposals means we have to keep an eye on him as an option.
McInerney continues his great start to the season with his fourth over 90 after 27 disposals and a goal this week.
McInerney is an interesting one as he kicked 3 and had a solid game. He hasn't averaged more than 88 in a season so he is a risk but could provide big reward.
Mills appeared to get hurt early but played on and posted his best score of the season with his 25 disposals.
Mills has been improving his output each week and was one of just two Swans in the 100 club this week.
Again we saw Rosas struggle to score as he had the lowest score for the Swans as just 35% of his 14 disposals were effective. He missed his low BE and the experiment is over.
Rosas couldn't replicate last week's heroics as he had just 7 disposals for his lowest score of the season.
Rosas kicked 7 goals from 11 kicks and 3 handballs. He isn't one we would bring in but a great game. For current owners his BE has dropped and should be rising for a couple of weeks.
Serong was back and made the most of the opportunity with his 4th best score for the season.
Serong struggled this week with 16 disposals at 68%. His BE has jumped to 60 meaning we are going to need to trade him fairly soon

Serong  had the equal most contested possessions in the game with 13 and he also posted his second best score of the season so far. Despite this his BE rose due to that big score dropping from his cycle
Serong had his equal lowest score of the season from his 13 disposals. His BE is now 64 with the 126 about to roll out of his cycle this week. So just beware of this.
Serong didn't post a huge one but he certainly did more than enough and with the big score from the previous week still in his cycle his BE remains negative.

Serong was massive with 90% TOG which was the third most for the Swans and he had 10 marks to go with his 27 disposals. He will have this in his cycle now for three games and he should rocket in value over that time.
Serong hasn't been bad and was just doing enough for us. Nothing to be concerned about yet. He has more money to make
Serong was solid again this week and he is still worth a hold with his 18 disposals and 84% time on ground.
Serong is a popular rookie choice and looked every part of it with a 19 possession game. He will be a popular selection despite his early bye.
Sheldrick needs to be traded out as he missed his BE by some distance.
Sheldrick spent a lot of time on the bench as he finished with just 51% time on ground. 21 disposals of which just 7 were kicks. This was his lowest since opening round.
22 disposals for Sheldrick with this his best score of the season so far. He has kept his BE low with this one.
Sheldrick posted his best for the year but has been suspended for 1 game for a high elbow hit. He isn't probably one that we want to target so if you are holding it may be time to trade.
With Gulden out we saw Sheldrick around the footy more and he recorded his second good outing in a row.
A few people interested in Sheldrick but despite having 23 disposals his efficiency really hurt him. He may not be one to start but certainly put on your watch list.
Warner went missing with just 19 points at the half but it was a big third term that got him to a respectable score.
18 touches and a goal for Warner with 11 contested possessions. His scores have been hovering around this area for the last 7 games.
Warner took a while to get going with just 9 points in the first quarter. He finished strong but his 21 disposals came at just 47% efficiency.
Warner was a very popular pick up this week with his price and bye coming into play. 20 disposals and 3 goals meant he made his BE and had his first ton of the season.
Chad has been good without being great. Not someone to bring in just yet.
Warner was seen in bursts during the game Another to watch but may not be in your starting squad.
Bont had a good first half but just 3 points in the third and 18 in the last for what was a down score for him and just his third under 100 for the year.

Bontempelli showed no sign of any injury as he tore up the game with 10 tackles 30 disposals and 7 clearances to be the clear difference. This makes it 3 over 150 this year. There has been talk of a rest but it doesn't look necessary after this week's game.

33 disposals and a couple of goals for Bont this week and his value has dropped and this is going to make him a popular target. His BE at 98 means you could get him in this week but one more week would be ok also.

Bont underwent a fitness test before the game and had his knee heavily strapped. However he had nothing to worry about. 29 disposals and a couple of goals. His BE has dropped to 160 so you may wait another week before launching.

Bont was tagged by Mullin and very successfully as Bont was held to just 14 disposals and his lowest score for the year and second low one in a row. His BE is now up at 238 meaning he will be very cheap in a couple of weeks.
Bont wasn't at his best with his 26 disposals coming at just 46% efficiency. This was his first under 110 and it has seen his BE rise to 179 which means he will get cheaper in a couple of weeks.

Bont was the trade in for the week that everyone wanted. He didn't let us down with his 35 disposals and 8 marks to go with a goal. It may be prudent to wait for his value to drop as he does have some tougher matchups in coming weeks.
Bont put the team on his back and really got them over the line in the last term to top the scoring in the game. He will be a must target post bye.
Bont was at his brilliant best despite attending less than half the CBAs. He has shown us that he will be someone we must get into our teams at some point.

Bont spent a reasonable amount of time up forward but with 3 goals still posted a good score. His BE will be high though as he was priced at 131. Another score of this level will see him get cheap and back into a more affordable price range.
Budarick posted his lowest score this season from his 16 disposals as his efficiency was down. He is still making money so good to hold.
Budarick returned to the side this week and didn't take the kick ins from Dale having just 1 but he made up for it with 10 marks and 23 disposals. A good hold for those that did.

Budarick continued his consistent start of the season with another in the 70s. His BE is slowly rising but will now miss the next 2 to 3 weeks through injury. He won't lose value so you can hold if you have other priorities.
Budarick seems to have settled in a scoring range that we would expect to see from him. He has some good money to make still and should keep his role in the side.
Despite this being his lowest he will still rise in value and make us money this season. Hold him through his bye.
Budarick has been a hot name in the preseason and he showed why with a 27 possession game with a goal. Will be a popular pick.
Buslinger's third game didn't deliver as those that brought him in had hoped. His score was about half of his average from the first two and his BE has now risen to 17.
Dale was the best scorer in the game with his 5th 100+ in a row and second over 140. 31 touches at 83% or him. He is looking back to that form of a couple of years ago where he was a must have.
Dale was one that many coaches targeted and with good reason. 25 disposals at 84% saw him post his third over 110 in a row.  His BE remains low at 53 so he could be a good one to get.
This is the Dale we saw at times during last season. 32 disposals and 7 marks at a handy 84%. Over the last four weeks we have seen better form from him.
Dale posted his best of the year in the loss. 25 kicks with 6 handballs to go with 10 contested possessions. Three of his last four have been over 100
Dale continues his up and down start to the year as he dropped back down to 74 this week. He isn't giving us the level of consistent high scoring we have seen in the past.
Much more like the Dale we are used to but we need to take into account it was against Essendon. Still a good confidence boost for him having 22 disposals at 100%.
It hasn't been a great start to the season for Dale's owners. This was his lowest so far and his value is dropping. He isn't someone we should be looking at until we see a turn around in form.
Dale hasn't really impressed this week. He doesn't have that freedom that he had last year and had 23 disposals with most of them uncontested.
Not the old Bailey Dale we have been used to so let's see how things settle down before we look to bring him in.
Darcy left the game in the second as his knee went underneath him. He has injured his ACL and will miss the season.
Darcy booted 3.3 from his 10 kicks so his score could have been much more.
4 goals for Darcy from his 16 disposals. Not a huge score compared to some team mates but a good one from a key forward.

English left the ground in the last after a head clash. He is going to miss this week after going into concussion protocols. Up until then he was having a good battle with Sweet having 20 hit outs and 19 disposals.
English returned and those that held wouldn't have been excited by his return of 15 disposals and 21 hit outs. He will be better for the run so next week he should be better.
English went down with what we now know is an MCL injury which will see him miss between 3 and 6 weeks. The club are hopeful it is at the low end but he is a trade for us regardless.
Another great score from English who had his hands full with McAndrew. He continues to show that he is one of the premier rucks this season and will be one you want to target if you don't have him.
English won the ruck contest against Briggs and Riccardi comfortably. We have now seen over the last two weeks that these new rules really suit him and he could be the pick of the rucks.
English didn't post the big score we saw in the preseason game but he was more than fine. He showed how he can exploit the new rules by being so mobile in this game. Worth considering as R1.
Jaques was on the trade table for a lot of teams and he ended with 17 disposals and beat his BE. But his new BE of 52 means you may want to move him on this week or next.
Jaques was quiet and made his BE ok but it was his lowest of the year. However with the Dogs injuries his spot in the side should be safe.
Jaques had his lowest score but it wasn't by much as he seems to have slipped into a scoring groove which should see him rise in value for a few weeks to come. Nothing to be concerned about.
Jaques has been very consistent so far this season and looks one of the safe rookies to be on the field for you.
One of the more popular selections in the preseason and he didn't disappoint as he filled up the stats and looks to be a great cash cow.
Jaques was another rookie that has become a lock with a big score and will have a great break even for his third game.
Artie Jones had his lowest score outside of opening round. He still made us money and has a new BE of 28. He looks to be solid in the team so we can use him in the byes but the cash gen won't be big.

Jones has been a popular trade in over the last two weeks and he did fine the footy on 16 occasions with this his second best score of the season. With the 21 out of his cycle now his BE remains low at 1.
Libba was concussed again and will now miss this week's game.
6 goals for Naughton in a very impressive display.  Just beware that he can have a very wide range of scoring week to week.
Richards did cop a bit of a knock early but was fine with his 19 disposals at just 57% due to the pressure of the Blues. His lowest score of the season.
Richards had 27 disposals with 6 clearances and 12 contested. This makes it 4 over 100 in the last 5 and he is certainly one to consider.
Richards was solid again as he has been bouncing around the 100 mark. A good return from last week.
Richards still doesn't look right but he still played 79% TOG but just the 18 disposals for his lowest score of the season so far.
After being in doubt again for this week Richards came out and top scored for the Dogs with his 13 tackles and 30 disposals. He didn't show any signs of discomfort.
Richards top scored and was the only Dog over 100 but he also suffered a knee issue that saw him helped from the ground. Watch the injury reports as he is a test.
Richards was a late out for the game with knee soreness but should be back for their Gather round clash.
Richards didn't back up that huge opening round game but still nothing to be concerned about. He simply allowed his captain to take the lion share this week.
Richards was the star for the Dogs and must be considered. He lifted his average by 12 last year and doesn't look like going backwards this season.
Sellwood had 13 disposals as he beat his BE but only just. His new BE of 58 is telling us it is time to have him on your trade out list. But you just may need him  during the byes.
Sellwood took 10 marks to go with his 17 disposals and is still handy and making money for us.
13 disposals for Sellwood as he now has a BE of 37 meaning he probably has one more week before we need to trade him.
Sellwood is still rising in value with some quality scoring this week. His last three have all been solid and fieldable.
Sellwood continues to beat his BE and laid 6 tackles. He is still ok and should be fine in the team with the injuries at the dogs.
Sellwood posted his best score of the season after a couple of quieter games which means that he has kept his BE low.
Sellwood struggled and his 7 possession game has seen his BE rise to 17 meaning he may have just one more week in your side
Good bounce back from Sellwood this week. With 6 marks and 16 disposals he has kept his BE negative so whilst he may not be one to play on field he is one you can keep through his bye.
Sellwood didn't excite us in this second outing. He came into a number of sides after opening round and we will need more than this to get him up and going as a cash cow.
CDT had a tough day with 1.3 from just 10 disposals. His scoring isn't enough to hold him.
CDT is now a must trade and is unfieldable with his last three all 55 or less.
Cooper had another tough game and he is losing value.  Move him on if you can.
This was always the concern with CDT in that he appears to have a longer term average in the 30-40 range with that one big score being an anomaly.
CDT came back to earth this week and posted his second lowest score showing us that previous week could have been a one off.

CDT was the only eagle to hit 100 in the win. This was a big turn around from the 37 in his first game. You can wait another week though if you want as it would be prudent to see another big score from the rookie.
CDT didn't do enough for us to warrant him in our teams as anything other than an R3 who won't make us enough cash to trade out.
Duursma had his lowest score of the season with his 20 disposals coming at 65%. Nothing to be concerned at however that BE has now risen to 85. He would be one of the last rookies to upgrade though.
Duursma just keeps rolling on. He is no longer a cash cow though as he won't make much more with his BE but he is still very much worth his spot on your team and is fieldable.
Duursma had the third best score for the Eagles this week from his 11 marks and 25 disposals. His BE remains manageable for him so keep riding him.

Was Duursma the one we missed? Yeah for most people as they baulked at his high price. Those that started him have been rewarded as he continues to post some great scores. His BE remains very achievable at 44.
Duursma continues to show us that he should have been in our teams despite the high price tag. He continues to impress and will be one you can possibly hold til his bye if he keeps this up.
Duursma had the fourth best score for the Eagles and was their only multiple goal kicker in the heavy loss to the Swans. This is a good sign that he can still score when the team is struggling.

Duursma has shown that paying up for him this year has been the right play as he recorded his first 100+ score. He could have gone higher as he kicked 3 behinds to go with his 1 goal and 20 disposals.
Duursma showed us why he was the number 1 pick with a second great score. His BE says you can still get him in as his price will rise after this week's game against the Power.

Duursma's first game was a tough one for his team but he did well with 14 disposals and 5 tackles. If you didn't start him you don't need to jump just yet. You can wait to see what happens next week still.
17 kicks and 2 handballs for Lindsay as he has taken either the most or equal most kick ins over 4 of the last 5 weeks and he played on every time.
Good game for Lindsay as he posted 24 disposals at 83%. He has been scoring well but with the 132 leaving his cycle this week that BE has risen to 80
Lindsay didn't have the huge score of last week but he still had a good outing with his value jumping on the back of his 17 disposal game. He should be good to hold til the byes.
Lindsay was huge with 31 disposals at 90% this week with one out of the box. His BE has now dropped to -24 meaning he will make some great cash over the coming weeks.
Lindsay continues to have some solid scoring with his 19 disposals and goal this week. He has a great BE still and is fieldable.
This was the best for the season for Lindsay which repaid owners who held him when he was dropped. His BE remains low so will make us some more cash now.
It was a tough day for the Eagles and this was reflected in Lindsay's score being his lowest. His BE was negative so no damage but when the Eagles lose big his score won't be high.
Lindsay returned to the side and rewarded those that held him with a handy 70 from 19 disposals. Just beware that the opposition should be tougher going forward.
Lindsay was dropped from the team which isn't a good sign. If you held and he isn't named this week then move him on.
Lindsay was heavily selected and was good with his 16 disposals. This was around the level scoring that we were expecting from him.
Lowest for the season for McCarthy. He missed his BE and his new one of 124 is a big issue.
McCarthy was the best for the Eagles from his 30 disposals. Back to back 100+ for the first time this year for him.
McCarthy picked up where he left off last season with another solid showing. He may not be one we get in yet but those that started him won't be too unhappy.
Wilmot was huge with 12 marks and 32 disposals. Easily his best of the year. But hold off until we see another game of this standard with his previous 5 only averaging 77.
Harley Reid not only went over 100 for three games in a row now but he posted a massive game with 34 disposals 8 tackles and 19 clearances and 10 clearances.
Reid had his first back to back scores over 100 this week from his 21 disposals coming at 81% and a goal. Importantly he gave away just the 1 free kick this week.
Harley posted his second over 100 for the season with his 26 disposals and 2 goals but it could have been so much more as he had 11 clangers and gave away 5 free kicks.

Reid was tagged by Garcia and had 19 of his 27 disposals by hand. He still led his team in clearances with 7. His scoring is not looking like reaching heights so this is about what we can expect from him.
Reid continues to give us middling type scores. He is going to find it tough in the Eagles side to score well unfortunately. 20 touches at 65% for him as it was tough in the Derby.
22 disposals and a goal for Harley to go with a goal. He is going to continue to get attention from the opposition and he seems to have settled in this scoring zone rather than going big.
Reid was tagged by Jordon for the game and became very frustrated ending with 17 disposals at 64%. He is susceptible to a tag so these scores could come more often.
Reid has put in his best score of the year which was aided by 2 goals. He is getting the highest CBAs for his side this year at 86%.
30 touches for Harley but 3 frees against and 9 clangers really dragged that score down.
Reid again had his issues with the umpires giving away 3 free kicks.

Dev Rob was back this week and had the third best score for the Eagles but he left the game late with a knee issue which was iced up. It has been revealed he has torn an ACL and now will miss the rest of the season. Trade.
Robertson will return this week from suspension so hopefully you held.
Robertson had the job blanketing Butters but following a dangerous tackle he will be missing this week. Given his money making potential he is one that we need to hold through this one week.
Dev Rob was again fantastic and he had the second most points for the Eagles. He is proving to be the great pick that we all suspected with a great role.
Robertson's first game for the Eagles was a good one with a huge 12 tackles. At his price he is a must have.
Shoenberg had 12 disposals but not enough points came from them.
One out of the box for Williams from 41 hit outs 2 goals 7 clearances and 9 tackles. This won't happen every week but if Darcy Cameron isn't back for Collingwood this week he could go big again.
Williams was better but you aren't going to want him in your side for too long.
We were worried about people trading him in after that good score and it turned out to be with good reason. Just 13 hitouts and 7 disposals for his 58.
Yeo was out of the game just before half time with a groin issue which is a real concern. If you have him then you need to trade him.
Derksen played his first game and posted 11 disposals and 4 marks. It wasn't a score that made us say we have to pick him but if he can do it
Zadow's first game saw just 3 disposals and 5 tackles. He doesn't look to be one we can consider.
Best of the season for Hollands with his 25 disposals and 2 goals. Just beware that his other two scores have been in the 60s.
Blamires posted just 13 disposals and missed his BE by some distance and has lost value. If he retains his spot in the side he must be traded.
Blamires finished with 16 disposals as he just got past his BE.  His new one of 60 is a problem as he is averaging 60 over the last three games.
Blamires came back in to the side this week and did make the most of it with 17 disposals. He made his BE comfortably but you need to move him on still.
16 kicks and 5 handballs for Blamires. His BE remains low this week with his lowest for the season about to drop out of his cycle. He is a hold
Blamires shook off last week's low score to get back to the range we have been used to seeing in his first three games.

Blamires didn't have a huge outing but his 15 disposals still sees his price rise despite this being his lowest of the season. Nothing to be concerned about but he may only have a few more weeks in our side.
Blamires gave us his best score of the season and ensured his BE remains negative and he will be a great cash cow for us.
Blamires is proving to be a great selection with his 16 disposals and 6 tackles this week. He is providing great scoring across these bye rounds.
Murdock posted his lowest score for the year which was due to his change in role where he tagged Whitfield for the game.  He had just 1 point in the first term. Hopefully this was a one off.
Murdock had his best score since his debut game with 25 disposals this week and 7 contested. This has seen his BE dropping to 30
Just the 16 touches for Murdock as he hasn't recaptured the form he had before his injury. His BE has jumped to 41 and this may force us to make a decision soon.
Murdock had his lowest but it was a poor game from the Eagles. 20 disposals for him and his cash generation has been slowed but certainly not stopped.
We had been waiting for a few weeks for Murdock to return. His great BE remains after his 8 tackles and 19 disposals delivered another high score.
Murdock was one of the highest traded in players this week and he didn't let us down with 92 points but will now miss 1-2 weeks with a hamstring injury.
Murdock came in for his first game and he top scored for the Eagles! You don't have to get him in this week but he must be on your watch list for after his second game.
Flynn Perez was dropped this week so we couldn't capitalise on his negative break even.
Perez had his lowest of the season but only just. He has been hanging around the 50s to 60s. His BE remains negative meaning you could still get him this week if you are in need of a def downgrade.
Burton copped a knock to his shoulder but did have 9 disposals. His score has seen his BE now rise sharply to 33 which isn't what we had hoped for from him.
Burton's third game netted just 9 disposals and his BE has now risen to -16. Not ideal for owners but if you do still want him he is still cheap.
